units.leftText: So when they came together, they asked Him, “Lord, will You at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?”

units.leftText: Jesus replied, “It is not for you to know times or seasons that the Father has fixed by His own authority.
units.rightText: And he said unto them, It is not for you to know times or seasons, which the Father hath set within his own authority.

units.leftText: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you will be My witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.”
units.rightText: But ye shall receive power, when the Holy Spirit is come upon you: and ye shall be my witnesses both in Jerusalem, and in all Judæa and Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

units.leftText: After He had said this, they watched as He was taken up, and a cloud hid Him from their sight.
units.rightText: And when he had said these things, as they were looking, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.

units.leftText: They were looking intently into the sky as He was going, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.
units.rightText: And while they were looking stedfastly into heaven as he went, behold two men stood by them in white apparel;

units.leftText: “Men of Galilee,” they said, “why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you have seen Him go into heaven.” Matthias Replaces Judas
units.rightText: who also said, Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye looking into heaven? this Jesus, who was received up from you into heaven, shall so come in like manner as ye beheld him going into heaven.

units.leftText: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives, which is near the city, a Sabbath day’s journey away.

units.leftText: When they arrived, they went to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.

units.leftText: With one accord they all continued in prayer, along with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.

units.leftText: “For it is written in the book of Psalms: ‘May his place be deserted; let there be no one to dwell in it,’ and, ‘May another take his position.’

units.rightText: Of the men therefore that have companied with us all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and went out among us,

units.leftText: So they proposed two men: Joseph called Barsabbas (also known as Justus) and Matthias.
units.rightText: And they put forward two, Joseph called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

units.leftText: And they prayed, “Lord, You know everyone’s heart. Show us which of these two You have chosen
units.rightText: And they prayed, and said, Thou, Lord, who knowest the hearts of all men, show of these two the one whom thou hast chosen,

units.leftText: Then they cast lots, and the lot fell to Matthias. So he was added to the eleven apostles.
units.rightText: And they gave lots for them; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.

units.leftText: When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place.
units.rightText: And when the day of Pentecost was now come, they were all together in one place.

units.rightText: whom God raised up, having loosed the pangs of death: because it was not possible that he should be holden of it.

units.leftText: But he was a prophet and knew that God had promised him on oath that He would place one of his descendants on his throne.

units.leftText: When the people heard this, they were cut to the heart and asked Peter and the other apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”
units.rightText: Now when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and the rest of the apostles, Brethren, what shall we do?

units.leftText: Peter replied, “Repent and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: And Peter said unto them, Repent ye, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ unto the remission of your sins; and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: This promise belongs to you and your children and to all who are far off — to all whom the Lord our God will call to Himself.”
units.rightText: For to you is the promise, and to your children, and to all that are afar off, even as many as the Lord our God shall call unto him.

units.leftText: With many other words he testified, and he urged them, “Be saved from this corrupt generation.”
units.rightText: And with many other words he testified, and exhorted them, saying, Save yourselves from this crooked generation.

units.leftText: And when he saw one of them being mistreated, Moses went to his defense and avenged him by striking down the Egyptian who was oppressing him.
units.rightText: And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, smiting the Egyptian:

units.leftText: He assumed his brothers would understand that God was using him to deliver them, but they did not.
units.rightText: and he supposed that his brethren understood that God by his hand was giving them deliverance; but they understood not.

units.leftText: The next day he came upon two Israelites who were fighting, and he tried to reconcile them, saying, ‘Men, you are brothers. Why are you mistreating each other?’
units.rightText: And the day following he appeared unto them as they strove, and would have set them at one again, saying, Sirs, ye are brethren; why do ye wrong one to another?

units.leftText: But the man who was abusing his neighbor pushed Moses aside and said, ‘Who made you ruler and judge over us?
units.rightText: But he that did his neighbor wrong thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge over us?

units.leftText: Do you want to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?’
units.rightText: Wouldest thou kill me, as thou killedst the Egyptian yesterday?
leftNotes: 7:28 Exodus 2:13–14|EXO 2:13-14* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: At this remark, Moses fled to the land of Midian, where he lived as a foreigner and had two sons. The Call of Moses (Exodus 3:1–22|EXO 3:1-22*)
units.rightText: And Moses fled at this saying, and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he begat two sons.

units.leftText: After forty years had passed, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
units.rightText: And when forty years were fulfilled, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.

units.leftText: When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight. As he approached to look more closely, the voice of the Lord came to him:
units.rightText: And when Moses saw it, he wondered at the sight: and as he drew near to behold, there came a voice of the Lord,

units.leftText: ‘I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.’ Moses trembled with fear and did not dare to look.
units.rightText: I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob. And Moses trembled, and durst not behold.
leftNotes: 7:32 Exodus 3:6|EXO 3:6*

units.leftText: Then the Lord said to him, ‘Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
units.rightText: And the Lord said unto him, Loose the shoes from thy feet: for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

units.leftText: I have indeed seen the oppression of My people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to deliver them. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.’
units.rightText: I have surely seen the affliction of my people that is in Egypt, and have heard their groaning, and I am come down to deliver them: and now come, I will send thee into Egypt.

units.leftText: This Moses, whom they had rejected with the words, ‘Who made you ruler and judge?’ is the one whom God sent to be their ruler and redeemer through the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
units.rightText: This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? him hath God sent to be both a ruler and a deliverer with the hand of the angel that appeared to him in the bush.
leftNotes: 7:35 Or Angel; also in verse 38

units.leftText: He led them out and performed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness.
units.rightText: This man led them forth, having wrought wonders and signs in Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness forty years.

units.leftText: This is the same Moses who told the Israelites, ‘God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your brothers.’
units.rightText: This is that Moses, who said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall God raise up unto you from among your brethren, like unto me.
leftNotes: 7:37 Deuteronomy 18:15|DEU 18:15*

units.leftText: He was in the assembly in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. And he received living words to pass on to us. The Rebellion of Israel (Exodus 32:1–35|EXO 32:1-35*; Deuteronomy 9:7–29|DEU 9:7-29*; Amos 5:16–27|AMO 5:16-27*)
units.rightText: This is he that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel that spake to him in the mount Sinai, and with our fathers: who received living oracles to give unto us:
leftNotes: 7:38 NE and WH to you

units.leftText: But our fathers refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.
units.rightText: to whom our fathers would not be obedient, but thrust him from them, and turned back in their hearts unto Egypt,

units.leftText: They said to Aaron, ‘Make us gods who will go before us! As for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.’
units.rightText: saying unto Aaron, Make us gods that shall go before us: for as for this Moses, who led us forth out of the land of Egypt, we know not what is become of him.

units.leftText: At that time they made a calf and offered a sacrifice to the idol, rejoicing in the works of their hands.
units.rightText: And they made a calf in those days, and brought a sacrifice unto the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands.

units.leftText: But God turned away from them and gave them over to the worship of the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: ‘Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
units.rightText: But God turned, and gave them up to serve the host of heaven; as it is written in the book of the prophets, Did ye offer unto me slain beasts and sacrifices Forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?

units.leftText: You have taken along the tabernacle of Molech and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Babylon.’ The Tabernacle of the Testimony (Exodus 40:1–33|EXO 40:1-33*; Hebrews 9:1–10|HEB 9:1-10*)
units.rightText: And ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, And the star of the god Rephan, The figures which ye made to worship them: And I will carry you away beyond Babylon.
leftNotes: 7:43 Amos 5:25–27|AMO 5:25-27* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the Testimony with them in the wilderness. It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.
units.rightText: Our fathers had the tabernacle of the testimony in the wilderness, even as he appointed who spake unto Moses, that he should make it according to the figure that he had seen.

units.leftText: And our fathers who received it brought it in with Joshua when they dispossessed the nations God drove out before them. It remained until the time of David,
units.rightText: Which also our fathers, in their turn, brought in with Joshua when they entered on the possession of the nations, that God thrust out before the face of our fathers, unto the days of David;

units.leftText: who found favor in the sight of God and asked to provide a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
units.rightText: who found favor in the sight of God, and asked to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.
leftNotes: 7:46 SBL, WH, BYZ, and TR; see also LXX for Psalm 132:5|PSA 132:5*; ECM and NE a dwelling place for the house of Jacob.

units.leftText: But it was Solomon who built the house for Him.
units.rightText: But Solomon built him a house.

units.leftText: However, the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says:
units.rightText: Howbeit the Most High dwelleth not in houses made with hands; as saith the prophet,

units.leftText: ‘Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or where will My place of repose be?
units.rightText: The heaven is my throne, And the earth the footstool of my feet: What manner of house will ye build me? saith the Lord: Or what is the place of my rest?

units.leftText: Has not My hand made all these things?’
units.rightText: Did not my hand make all these things?

units.leftText: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears! You always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did.
units.rightText: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Spirit: as your fathers did, so do ye.

units.leftText: Which of the prophets did your fathers fail to persecute? They even killed those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One. And now you are His betrayers and murderers —
units.rightText: Which of the prophets did not your fathers persecute? and they killed them that showed before of the coming of the Righteous One; of whom ye have now become betrayers and murderers;

units.leftText: you who received the law ordained by angels, yet have not kept it.” The Stoning of Stephen
units.rightText: ye who received the law as it was ordained by angels, and kept it not.

units.leftText: On hearing this, the members of the Sanhedrin were enraged, and they gnashed their teeth at him.
units.rightText: Now when they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.
leftNotes: 7:54 Literally On hearing these things, they were cut in their hearts,

units.leftText: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
units.rightText: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God,

units.leftText: “Look,” he said, “I see heaven open and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”
units.rightText: and said, Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing on the right hand of God.

units.leftText: At this they covered their ears, cried out in a loud voice, and rushed together at him.
units.rightText: But they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and rushed upon him with one accord;

units.leftText: They dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
units.rightText: and they cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.

units.leftText: While they were stoning him, Stephen appealed, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.”
units.rightText: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon the Lord, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.

units.leftText: Falling on his knees, he cried out in a loud voice, “Lord, do not hold this sin against them.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
units.rightText: And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

units.leftText: And Saul was there, giving approval to Stephen’s death.
units.rightText: And Saul was consenting unto his death. And there arose on that day a great persecution against the church which was in Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judæa and Samaria, except the apostles.

units.leftText: God-fearing men buried Stephen and mourned deeply over him.
units.rightText: And devout men buried Stephen, and made great lamentation over him.

units.leftText: But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off men and women and put them in prison. Philip in Samaria
units.rightText: But Saul laid waste the church, entering into every house, and dragging men and women committed them to prison.

units.leftText: Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.
units.rightText: They therefore that were scattered abroad went about preaching the word.

units.leftText: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and proclaimed the Christ to them.
units.rightText: And Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and proclaimed unto them the Christ.

units.leftText: The crowds all paid close attention to Philip’s message and to the signs they saw him perform.
units.rightText: And the multitudes gave heed with one accord unto the things that were spoken by Philip, when they heard, and saw the signs which he did.

units.leftText: With loud shrieks, unclean spirits came out of many who were possessed, and many of the paralyzed and lame were healed.
units.rightText: For from many of those that had unclean spirits, they came out, crying with a loud voice: and many that were palsied, and that were lame, were healed.

units.leftText: So there was great joy in that city. Simon the Sorcerer (Deuteronomy 18:9–14|DEU 18:9-14*)
units.rightText: And there was much joy in that city.

units.leftText: Prior to that time, a man named Simon had practiced sorcery in the city and astounded the people of Samaria. He claimed to be someone great,
units.rightText: But there was a certain man, Simon by name, who beforetime in the city used sorcery, and amazed the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one:

units.leftText: and all the people, from the least to the greatest, heeded his words and said, “This man is the divine power called the Great Power.”
units.rightText: to whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is that power of God which is called Great.

units.leftText: They paid close attention to him because he had astounded them for a long time with his sorcery.
units.rightText: And they gave heed to him, because that of long time he had amazed them with his sorceries.

units.leftText: But when they believed Philip as he preached the gospel of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
units.rightText: But when they believed Philip preaching good tidings concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.

units.leftText: Even Simon himself believed and was baptized. He followed Philip closely and was astounded by the great signs and miracles he observed.
units.rightText: And Simon also himself believed: and being baptized, he continued with Philip; and beholding signs and great miracles wrought, he was amazed.

units.leftText: When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
units.rightText: Now when the apostles that were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:

units.leftText: On their arrival, they prayed for them to receive the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Spirit:

units.leftText: For the Holy Spirit had not yet fallen upon any of them; they had simply been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: for as yet it was fallen upon none of them: only they had been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

units.leftText: Then Peter and John laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: When Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money.
units.rightText: Now when Simon saw that through the laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Spirit was given, he offered them money,

units.leftText: “Give me this power as well,” he said, “so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.”
units.rightText: saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay my hands, he may receive the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: But Peter replied, “May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!
units.rightText: But Peter said unto him, Thy silver perish with thee, because thou hast thought to obtain the gift of God with money.

units.leftText: You have no part or share in our ministry, because your heart is not right before God.
units.rightText: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right before God.

units.leftText: Repent, therefore, of your wickedness, and pray to the Lord. Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart.
units.rightText: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray the Lord, if perhaps the thought of thy heart shall be forgiven thee.

units.leftText: For I see that you are poisoned by bitterness and captive to iniquity.”
units.rightText: For I see that thou art in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity.

units.leftText: Then Simon answered, “Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.”
units.rightText: And Simon answered and said, Pray ye for me to the Lord, that none of the things which ye have spoken come upon me.

units.leftText: And after Peter and John had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many of the Samaritan villages. Philip and the Ethiopian (Isaiah 53:1–8|ISA 53:1-8*)
units.rightText: They therefore, when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel to many villages of the Samaritans.

units.leftText: Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip, “Get up and go south to the desert road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.”
units.rightText: But an angel of the Lord spake unto Philip, saying, Arise, and go toward the south unto the way that goeth down from Jerusalem unto Gaza: the same is desert.

units.leftText: So he started out, and on his way he met an Ethiopian eunuch, a court official in charge of the entire treasury of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,
units.rightText: And he arose and went: and behold, a man of Ethiopia, a eunuch of great authority under Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasure, who had come to Jerusalem to worship;
leftNotes: 8:27 Greek Kandakē

units.leftText: and on his return was sitting in his chariot reading Isaiah the prophet.
units.rightText: and he was returning and sitting in his chariot, and was reading the prophet Isaiah.

units.leftText: The Spirit said to Philip, “Go over to that chariot and stay by it.”
units.rightText: And the Spirit said unto Philip, Go near, and join thyself to this chariot.

units.leftText: So Philip ran up and heard the man reading Isaiah the prophet. “Do you understand what you are reading?” Philip asked.
units.rightText: And Philip ran to him, and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, Understandest thou what thou readest?

units.leftText: “How can I,” he said, “unless someone guides me?” And he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
units.rightText: And he said, How can I, except some one shall guide me? And he besought Philip to come up and sit with him.

units.leftText: The eunuch was reading this passage of Scripture: “He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and as a lamb before the shearer is silent, so He did not open His mouth.
units.rightText: Now the passage of the scripture which he was reading was this, He was led as a sheep to the slaughter; And as a lamb before his shearer is dumb, So he openeth not his mouth:

units.leftText: In His humiliation He was deprived of justice. Who can recount His descendants? For His life was removed from the earth.”
units.rightText: In his humiliation his judgment was taken away: His generation who shall declare? For his life is taken from the earth.
leftNotes: 8:33 Isaiah 53:7–8|ISA 53:7-8* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: “Tell me,” said the eunuch, “who is the prophet talking about, himself or someone else?”
units.rightText: And the eunuch answered Philip, and said, I pray thee, of whom speaketh the prophet this? of himself, or of some other?

units.leftText: Then Philip began with this very Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
units.rightText: And Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this scripture, preached unto him Jesus.

units.leftText: As they traveled along the road and came to some water, the eunuch said, “Look, here is water! What is there to prevent me from being baptized?”
units.rightText: And as they went on the way, they came unto a certain water; and the eunuch saith, Behold, here is water; what doth hinder me to be baptized?
leftNotes: 8:36 TR includes 37*And Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may be baptized.” The eunuch replied, “I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.”

rightNotes: 8:37 Some ancient authorities insert, wholly or in part, v. 37. And Philip said, If thou believest with all thy heart, thou mayest. And he answered and said, I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.

units.leftText: And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the eunuch went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
units.rightText: And he commanded the chariot to stand still: and they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.

units.leftText: When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord carried Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, but went on his way rejoicing.
units.rightText: And when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip; and the eunuch saw him no more, for he went on his way rejoicing.

units.leftText: But Philip appeared at Azotus and traveled through that region, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he came to Caesarea.
units.rightText: But Philip was found at Azotus: and passing through he preached the gospel to all the cities, till he came to Cæsarea.

units.leftText: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord. He approached the high priest
units.rightText: But Saul, yet breathing threatening and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,

units.leftText: and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to the Way, he could bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: and asked of him letters to Damascus unto the synagogues, that if he found any that were of the Way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
units.rightText: And as he journeyed, it came to pass that he drew nigh unto Damascus: and suddenly there shone round about him a light out of heaven:

units.leftText: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”
units.rightText: and he fell upon the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

units.leftText: “Who are You, Lord?” Saul asked.
units.rightText: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And he said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest:

units.leftText: “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”
units.rightText: but rise, and enter into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.

units.leftText: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the voice but did not see anyone.
units.rightText: And the men that journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing the voice, but beholding no man.

units.leftText: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could not see a thing. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.
units.rightText: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw nothing; and they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.
leftNotes: 9:8 Literally he could see nothing or he could see no one

units.leftText: For three days he was without sight, and he did not eat or drink anything. Ananias Baptizes Saul
units.rightText: And he was three days without sight, and did neither eat nor drink.

units.leftText: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision, “Ananias!” “Here I am, Lord,” he answered.
units.rightText: Now there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and the Lord said unto him in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord.

units.leftText: “Get up!” the Lord told him. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.
units.rightText: And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go to the street which is called Straight, and inquire in the house of Judas for one named Saul, a man of Tarsus: for behold, he prayeth;

units.leftText: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.”
units.rightText: and he hath seen a man named Ananias coming in, and laying his hands on him, that he might receive his sight.

units.leftText: But Ananias answered, “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: But Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard from many of this man, how much evil he did to thy saints at Jerusalem:

units.leftText: And now he is here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.”
units.rightText: and here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call upon thy name.

units.leftText: “Go!” said the Lord. “This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name before the Gentiles and their kings, and before the people of Israel.
units.rightText: But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles and kings, and the children of Israel:

units.leftText: I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”
units.rightText: for I will show him how many things he must suffer for my name’s sake.

units.leftText: So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul. “Brother Saul,” he said, “the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”
units.rightText: And Ananias departed, and entered into the house; and laying his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, who appeared unto thee in the way which thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mayest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: At that instant, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and his sight was restored. He got up and was baptized,
units.rightText: And straightway there fell from his eyes as it were scales, and he received his sight; and he arose and was baptized;

units.leftText: and after taking some food, he regained his strength. And he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus. Saul Preaches at Damascus
units.rightText: and he took food and was strengthened. And he was certain days with the disciples that were at Damascus.

units.leftText: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, declaring, “He is the Son of God.”
units.rightText: And straightway in the synagogues he proclaimed Jesus, that he is the Son of God.

units.leftText: All who heard him were astounded and asked, “Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name? And hasn’t he come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?”
units.rightText: And all that heard him were amazed, and said, Is not this he that in Jerusalem made havoc of them that called on this name? and he had come hither for this intent, that he might bring them bound before the chief priests.

units.leftText: But Saul was empowered all the more, and he confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ. The Escape from Damascus
units.rightText: But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews that dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ.

units.leftText: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,
units.rightText: And when many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel together to kill him:

units.leftText: but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.
units.rightText: but their plot became known to Saul. And they watched the gates also day and night that they might kill him:

units.leftText: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall. Saul in Jerusalem
units.rightText: but his disciples took him by night, and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
leftNotes: 9:25 Literally through the wall; see 2 Corinthians 11:33|2CO 11:33*.

units.leftText: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
units.rightText: And when he was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: and they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

units.leftText: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who had spoken to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.
units.rightText: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how at Damascus he had preached boldly in the name of Jesus.

units.leftText: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
units.rightText: And he was with them going in and going out at Jerusalem,

units.leftText: He talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him.
units.rightText: preaching boldly in the name of the Lord: and he spake and disputed against the Grecian Jews; but they were seeking to kill him.
leftNotes: 9:29 Or Hellenists

units.leftText: When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus. The Healing of Aeneas
units.rightText: And when the brethren knew it, they brought him down to Cæsarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.

units.leftText: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria experienced a time of peace. It grew in strength and numbers, living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: So the church throughout all Judæa and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being edified; and, walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, was multiplied.

units.leftText: As Peter traveled throughout the area, he went to visit the saints in Lydda.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as Peter went throughout all parts, he came down also to the saints that dwelt at Lydda.

units.leftText: There he found a man named Aeneas who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.
units.rightText: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had kept his bed eight years; for he was palsied.

units.leftText: “Aeneas,” Peter said to him, “Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and put away your mat.” Immediately Aeneas got up,
units.rightText: And Peter said unto him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ healeth thee: arise, and make thy bed. And straightway he arose.

units.leftText: and all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord. The Raising of Tabitha (John 11:38–44|JHN 11:38-44*)
units.rightText: And all that dwelt at Lydda and in Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.

units.leftText: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which is translated as Dorcas), who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.
units.rightText: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.
leftNotes: 9:36 Tabitha in Aramaic and Dorcas in Greek both mean gazelle.

units.leftText: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in those days, that she fell sick, and died: and when they had washed her, they laid her in an upper chamber.

units.leftText: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to urge him, “Come to us without delay.”
units.rightText: And as Lydda was nigh unto Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men unto him, entreating him, Delay not to come on unto us.

units.leftText: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
units.rightText: And Peter arose and went with them. And when he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and showing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.

units.leftText: Then Peter sent them all out of the room. He knelt down and prayed, and turning toward her body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
units.rightText: But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning to the body, he said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes; and when she saw Peter, she sat up.

units.leftText: Peter took her by the hand and helped her up. Then he called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive.
units.rightText: And he gave her his hand, and raised her up; and calling the saints and widows, he presented her alive.

units.leftText: This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
units.rightText: And it became known throughout all Joppa: and many believed on the Lord.

units.leftText: And Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that he abode many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner.

units.leftText: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment.
units.rightText: Now there was a certain man in Cæsarea, Cornelius by name, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,

units.leftText: He and all his household were devout and God-fearing. He gave generously to the people and prayed to God regularly.
units.rightText: a devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, who gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God always.

units.leftText: One day at about the ninth hour, he had a clear vision of an angel of God who came to him and said, “Cornelius!”
units.rightText: He saw in a vision openly, as it were about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in unto him, and saying to him, Cornelius.
leftNotes: 10:3 That is, about three in the afternoon; also in verse 30

units.leftText: Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked, “What is it, Lord?”
units.rightText: And he, fastening his eyes upon him, and being affrighted, said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are gone up for a memorial before God.

units.leftText: Now send men to Joppa to call for a man named Simon who is called Peter.
units.rightText: And now send men to Joppa, and fetch one Simon, who is surnamed Peter:

units.leftText: He is staying with Simon the tanner, whose house is by the sea. ”
units.rightText: he lodgeth with one Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea side.
leftNotes: 10:6 TR includes He will tell you what you need to do.

units.leftText: When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a devout soldier from among his attendants.
units.rightText: And when the angel that spake unto him was departed, he called two of his household-servants, and a devout soldier of them that waited on him continually;

units.leftText: He explained what had happened and sent them to Joppa. Peter’s Vision (Leviticus 11:1–47|LEV 11:1-47*; Deuteronomy 14:1–21|DEU 14:1-21*)
units.rightText: and having rehearsed all things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.

units.leftText: The next day at about the sixth hour, as the men were approaching the city on their journey, Peter went up on the roof to pray.
units.rightText: Now on the morrow, as they were on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour:
leftNotes: 10:9 That is, about noon

units.leftText: He became hungry and wanted something to eat, but while the meal was being prepared, he fell into a trance.
units.rightText: and he became hungry, and desired to eat: but while they made ready, he fell into a trance;

units.leftText: He saw heaven open and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.
units.rightText: and he beholdeth the heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending, as it were a great sheet, let down by four corners upon the earth:

units.leftText: It contained all kinds of four-footed animals and reptiles of the earth, as well as birds of the air.
units.rightText: wherein were all manner of fourfooted beasts and creeping things of the earth and birds of the heaven.

units.leftText: Then a voice said to him: “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!”
units.rightText: And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill and eat.

units.leftText: “No, Lord!” Peter answered. “I have never eaten anything impure or unclean.”
units.rightText: But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten anything that is common and unclean.
leftNotes: 10:14 Literally common; similarly in verses 15 and 28

units.leftText: The voice spoke to him a second time: “Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.”
units.rightText: And a voice came unto him again the second time, What God hath cleansed, make not thou common.

units.leftText: This happened three times, and all at once the sheet was taken back up into heaven. Peter Called to Caesarea
units.rightText: And this was done thrice: and straightway the vessel was received up into heaven.

units.leftText: While Peter was puzzling over the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found Simon’s house and approached the gate.
units.rightText: Now while Peter was much perplexed in himself what the vision which he had seen might mean, behold, the men that were sent by Cornelius, having made inquiry for Simon’s house, stood before the gate,

units.leftText: They called out to ask if Simon called Peter was staying there.
units.rightText: and called and asked whether Simon, who was surnamed Peter, were lodging there.

units.leftText: As Peter continued to reflect on the vision, the Spirit said to him, “Behold, three men are looking for you.
units.rightText: And while Peter thought on the vision, the Spirit said unto him, Behold, three men seek thee.
leftNotes: 10:19 ECM and TR; NE and WH two men are looking for you; SBL and BYZ men are looking for you

units.leftText: So get up! Go downstairs and accompany them without hesitation, because I have sent them.”
units.rightText: But arise, and get thee down, and go with them, nothing doubting: for I have sent them.

units.leftText: So Peter went down to the men and said, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?”
units.rightText: And Peter went down to the men, and said, Behold, I am he whom ye seek: what is the cause wherefore ye are come?
leftNotes: 10:21 TR the men sent to him by Cornelius

units.leftText: “Cornelius the centurion has sent us,” they said. “He is a righteous and God-fearing man with a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation. A holy angel instructed him to request your presence in his home so he could hear a message from you.”
units.rightText: And they said, Cornelius a centurion, a righteous man and one that feareth God, and well reported of by all the nation of the Jews, was warned of God by a holy angel to send for thee into his house, and to hear words from thee.

units.leftText: So Peter invited them in as his guests. And the next day he got ready and went with them, accompanied by some of the brothers from Joppa. Peter Visits Cornelius
units.rightText: So he called them in and lodged them. And on the morrow he arose and went forth with them, and certain of the brethren from Joppa accompanied him.

units.leftText: The following day he arrived in Caesarea, where Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
units.rightText: And on the morrow they entered into Cæsarea. And Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his kinsmen and his near friends.

units.leftText: As Peter was about to enter, Cornelius met him and fell at his feet to worship him.
units.rightText: And when it came to pass that Peter entered, Cornelius met him, and fell down at his feet, and worshipped him.

units.leftText: But Peter helped him up. “Stand up,” he said, “I am only a man myself.”
units.rightText: But Peter raised him up, saying, Stand up; I myself also am a man.

units.leftText: As Peter talked with him, he went inside and found many people gathered together.
units.rightText: And as he talked with him, he went in, and findeth many come together:

units.leftText: He said to them, “You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean.
units.rightText: and he said unto them, Ye yourselves know how it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Jew to join himself or come unto one of another nation; and yet unto me hath God showed that I should not call any man common or unclean:

units.leftText: So when I was invited, I came without objection. I ask, then, why have you sent for me?”
units.rightText: wherefore also I came without gainsaying, when I was sent for. I ask therefore with what intent ye sent for me.

units.leftText: Cornelius answered: “Four days ago I was in my house praying at this, the ninth hour. Suddenly a man in radiant clothing stood before me
units.rightText: And Cornelius said, Four days ago, until this hour, I was keeping the ninth hour of prayer in my house; and behold, a man stood before me in bright apparel,
leftNotes: 10:30 BYZ and TR Four days ago I was fasting until this hour, and at the ninth hour I was praying in my house.

units.leftText: and said, ‘Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God.
units.rightText: and saith, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine alms are had in remembrance in the sight of God.

units.leftText: Therefore send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea.’
units.rightText: Send therefore to Joppa, and call unto thee Simon, who is surnamed Peter; he lodgeth in the house of Simon a tanner, by the sea side.

units.leftText: So I sent for you immediately, and you were kind enough to come. Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us.” Good News for the Gentiles
units.rightText: Forthwith therefore I sent to thee; and thou hast well done that thou art come. Now therefore we are all here present in the sight of God, to hear all things that have been commanded thee of the Lord.

units.leftText: Then Peter began to speak: “I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism,
units.rightText: And Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons:

units.leftText: but welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right.
units.rightText: but in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is acceptable to him.

units.leftText: He has sent this message to the people of Israel, proclaiming the gospel of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
units.rightText: The word which he sent unto the children of Israel, preaching good tidings of peace by Jesus Christ (he is Lord of all)—

units.leftText: You yourselves know what has happened throughout Judea, beginning in Galilee with the baptism that John proclaimed:
units.rightText: that saying ye yourselves know, which was published throughout all Judæa, beginning from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached;

units.leftText: how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power, and how Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.
units.rightText: even Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.

units.leftText: We are witnesses of all that He did, both in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. And although they put Him to death by hanging Him on a tree,
units.rightText: And we are witnesses of all things which he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; whom also they slew, hanging him on a tree.

units.leftText: God raised Him up on the third day and caused Him to be seen —
units.rightText: Him God raised up the third day, and gave him to be made manifest,

units.leftText: not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand, by us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
units.rightText: not to all the people, but unto witnesses that were chosen before of God, even to us, who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead.

units.leftText: And He commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that He is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead.
units.rightText: And he charged us to preach unto the people, and to testify that this is he who is ordained of God to be the Judge of the living and the dead.

units.leftText: All the prophets testify about Him that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.” The Gentiles Receive the Holy Spirit (Acts 19:1–7|ACT 19:1-7*)
units.rightText: To him bear all the prophets witness, that through his name every one that believeth on him shall receive remission of sins.

units.leftText: While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message.
units.rightText: While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Spirit fell on all them that heard the word.

units.leftText: All the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles.
units.rightText: And they of the circumcision that believed were amazed, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: For they heard them speaking in tongues and exalting God.
units.rightText: For they heard them speak with tongues, and magnify God. Then answered Peter,

units.leftText: “Can anyone withhold the water to baptize these people? They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!”
units.rightText: Can any man forbid the water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit as well as we?

units.leftText: So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to stay for a few days.
units.rightText: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.

units.leftText: The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
units.rightText: Now the apostles and the brethren that were in Judæa heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.

units.leftText: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers took issue with him
units.rightText: And when Peter was come up to Jerusalem, they that were of the circumcision contended with him,
leftNotes: 11:2 Literally those of the circumcision

units.leftText: and said, “You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them.”
units.rightText: saying, Thou wentest in to men uncircumcised, and didst eat with them.

units.leftText: But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events:
units.rightText: But Peter began, and expounded the matter unto them in order, saying,

units.leftText: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.
units.rightText: I was in the city of Joppa praying: and in a trance I saw a vision, a certain vessel descending, as it were a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners; and it came even unto me:

units.leftText: I looked at it closely and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.
units.rightText: upon which when I had fastened mine eyes, I considered, and saw the fourfooted beasts of the earth and wild beasts and creeping things and birds of the heaven.

units.leftText: Then I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter, kill and eat.’
units.rightText: And I heard also a voice saying unto me, Rise, Peter; kill and eat.

units.leftText: ‘No, Lord,’ I said, ‘for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
units.rightText: But I said, Not so, Lord: for nothing common or unclean hath ever entered into my mouth.
leftNotes: 11:8 Literally common; similarly in verse 9

units.leftText: But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.’
units.rightText: But a voice answered the second time out of heaven, What God hath cleansed, make not thou common.

units.leftText: This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.
units.rightText: And this was done thrice: and all were drawn up again into heaven.

units.leftText: Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
units.rightText: And behold, forthwith three men stood before the house in which we were, having been sent from Cæsarea unto me.

units.leftText: The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.
units.rightText: And the Spirit bade me go with them, making no distinction. And these six brethren also accompanied me; and we entered into the man’s house:

units.leftText: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.
units.rightText: and he told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house, and saying, Send to Joppa, and fetch Simon, whose surname is Peter;

units.leftText: He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’
units.rightText: who shall speak unto thee words, whereby thou shalt be saved, thou and all thy house.

units.leftText: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.
units.rightText: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.

units.leftText: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, how He said, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
units.rightText: And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said, John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit.
leftNotes: 11:16 Or ‘John baptized in water, but in a few days you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’Acts 1:5|ACT 1:5*

units.leftText: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”
units.rightText: If then God gave unto them the like gift as he did also unto us, when we believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?

units.leftText: When they heard this, they had no further objections, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.” The Church at Antioch
units.rightText: And when they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then to the Gentiles also hath God granted repentance unto life.

units.leftText: Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.
units.rightText: They therefore that were scattered abroad upon the tribulation that arose about Stephen travelled as far as Phoenicia, and Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to none save only to Jews.

units.leftText: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they were come to Antioch, spake unto the Greeks also, preaching the Lord Jesus.
leftNotes: 11:20 Or the Hellenists

units.leftText: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
units.rightText: And the hand of the Lord was with them: and a great number that believed turned unto the Lord.

units.leftText: When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
units.rightText: And the report concerning them came to the ears of the church which was in Jerusalem: and they sent forth Barnabas as far as Antioch:

units.leftText: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.
units.rightText: who, when he was come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad; and he exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord:

units.leftText: Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
units.rightText: for he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith: and much people was added unto the Lord.

units.leftText: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
units.rightText: And he went forth to Tarsus to seek for Saul;

units.leftText: and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
units.rightText: and when he had found him, he brought him unto Antioch. And it came to pass, that even for a whole year they were gathered together with the church, and taught much people; and that the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.

units.leftText: In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
units.rightText: Now in these days there came down prophets from Jerusalem unto Antioch.

units.leftText: One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. ( This happened under Claudius.)
units.rightText: And there stood up one of them named Agabus, and signified by the Spirit that there should be a great famine over all the world: which came to pass in the days of Claudius.
leftNotes: 11:28 Or the entire Roman world

units.leftText: So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
units.rightText: And the disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief unto the brethren that dwelt in Judæa:

units.leftText: This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.
units.rightText: which also they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

units.leftText: About that time, King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church.
units.rightText: Now about that time Herod the king put forth his hands to afflict certain of the church.
leftNotes: 12:1 That is, King Herod Agrippa
12:1 Literally put forth the hands to mistreat

units.leftText: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.
units.rightText: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.

units.leftText: And seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod proceeded to seize Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
units.rightText: And when he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to seize Peter also. And those were the days of unleavened bread.
leftNotes: 12:3 Literally seize Peter—now these were the days of the Unleavened; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover. The Rescue of Peter
units.rightText: And when he had taken him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to guard him; intending after the Passover to bring him forth to the people.

units.leftText: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was fervently praying to God for him.
units.rightText: Peter therefore was kept in the prison: but prayer was made earnestly of the church unto God for him.

units.leftText: On the night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with sentries standing guard at the entrance to the prison.
units.rightText: And when Herod was about to bring him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and guards before the door kept the prison.

units.leftText: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.
units.rightText: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shined in the cell: and he smote Peter on the side, and awoke him, saying, Rise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.

units.leftText: “Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”
units.rightText: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And he did so. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.

units.leftText: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.
units.rightText: And he went out, and followed; and he knew not that it was true which was done by the angel, but thought he saw a vision.

units.leftText: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.
units.rightText: And when they were past the first and the second guard, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth into the city; which opened to them of its own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and straightway the angel departed from him.

units.leftText: Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”
units.rightText: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a truth, that the Lord hath sent forth his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.

units.leftText: And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.
units.rightText: And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together and were praying.

units.leftText: He knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.
units.rightText: And when he knocked at the door of the gate, a maid came to answer, named Rhoda.

units.leftText: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside and announced, “Peter is standing at the gate!”
units.rightText: And when she knew Peter’s voice, she opened not the gate for joy, but ran in, and told that Peter stood before the gate.

units.leftText: “You are out of your mind,” they told her. But when she kept insisting it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.”
units.rightText: And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she confidently affirmed that it was even so. And they said, It is his angel.

units.leftText: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.
units.rightText: But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened, they saw him, and were amazed.

units.leftText: Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.
units.rightText: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him forth out of the prison. And he said, Tell these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went to another place.

units.leftText: At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.
units.rightText: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.

units.leftText: After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there. The Death of Herod
units.rightText: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the guards, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judæa to Cæsarea, and tarried there.

units.leftText: Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king’s country for food.
units.rightText: Now he was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: and they came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus the king’s chamberlain their friend, they asked for peace, because their country was fed from the king’s country.

units.rightText: Now Paul and his company set sail from Paphos, and came to Perga in Pamphylia: and John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: And from Perga, they traveled inland to Pisidian Antioch, where they entered the synagogue on the Sabbath and sat down.
units.rightText: But they, passing through from Perga, came to Antioch of Pisidia; and they went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and sat down.

units.leftText: After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them: “Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.”
units.rightText: And after the reading of the law and the prophets the rulers of the synagogue sent unto them, saying, Brethren, if ye have any word of exhortation for the people, say on.

units.leftText: Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and began to speak: “Men of Israel and you Gentiles who fear God, listen to me!
units.rightText: And Paul stood up, and beckoning with the hand said, Men of Israel, and ye that fear God, hearken:

units.leftText: The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers. He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of that land.
units.rightText: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they sojourned in the land of Egypt, and with a high arm led he them forth out of it.

units.leftText: He endured their conduct for about forty years in the wilderness.
units.rightText: And for about the time of forty years as a nursing-father bare he them in the wilderness.

units.leftText: And having vanquished seven nations in Canaan, He gave their land to His people as an inheritance.
units.rightText: And when he had destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave them their land for an inheritance, for about four hundred and fifty years:

units.leftText: Then the people asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin, who ruled forty years.
units.rightText: And afterward they asked for a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for the space of forty years.

units.leftText: After removing Saul, He raised up David as their king and testified about him: ‘I have found David son of Jesse a man after My own heart; he will carry out My will in its entirety.’
units.rightText: And when he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king; to whom also he bare witness and said, I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after my heart, who shall do all my will.

units.leftText: From the descendants of this man, God has brought to Israel the Savior Jesus, as He promised.
units.rightText: Of this man’s seed hath God according to promise brought unto Israel a Saviour, Jesus;

units.rightText: when John had first preached before his coming the baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

units.leftText: As John was completing his course, he said, ‘Who do you suppose I am? I am not that One. But there is One coming after me whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.’
units.rightText: And as John was fulfilling his course, he said, What suppose ye that I am? I am not he. But behold, there cometh one after me the shoes of whose feet I am not worthy to unloose.

units.leftText: Brothers, children of Abraham, and you Gentiles who fear God, it is to us that this message of salvation has been sent.
units.rightText: Brethren, children of the stock of Abraham, and those among you that fear God, to us is the word of this salvation sent forth.

units.leftText: The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus, yet in condemning Him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
units.rightText: For they that dwell in Jerusalem, and their rulers, because they knew him not, nor the voices of the prophets which are read every sabbath, fulfilled them by condemning him.

units.leftText: And though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have Him executed.
units.rightText: And though they found no cause of death in him, yet asked they of Pilate that he should be slain.

units.leftText: When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.
units.rightText: And when they had fulfilled all things that were written of him, they took him down from the tree, and laid him in a tomb.

units.leftText: But God raised Him from the dead,
units.rightText: But God raised him from the dead:

units.rightText: and he was seen for many days of them that came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses unto the people.

units.leftText: And now we proclaim to you the good news: What God promised our fathers
units.rightText: And we bring you good tidings of the promise made unto the fathers,

units.rightText: that God hath fulfilled the same unto our children, in that he raised up Jesus; as also it is written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.

units.leftText: In fact, God raised Him from the dead, never to see decay. As He has said: ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.’
units.rightText: And as concerning that he raised him up from the dead, now no more to return to corruption, he hath spoken on this wise, I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.

units.leftText: But the One whom God raised from the dead did not see decay.

units.leftText: Therefore let it be known to you, brothers, that through Jesus the forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you.
units.rightText: Be it known unto you therefore, brethren, that through this man is proclaimed unto you remission of sins:

units.leftText: Through Him everyone who believes is justified from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses.
units.rightText: and by him every one that believeth is justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.

units.rightText: Beware therefore, lest that come upon you which is spoken in the prophets:

units.rightText: Behold, ye despisers, and wonder, and perish; For I work a work in your days, A work which ye shall in no wise believe, if one declare it unto you.
