units.leftText: As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people urged them to continue this message on the next Sabbath.
units.rightText: And as they went out, they besought that these words might be spoken to them the next sabbath.

units.leftText: After the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and urged them to continue in the grace of God.
units.rightText: Now when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas; who, speaking to them, urged them to continue in the grace of God.

units.leftText: On the following Sabbath, nearly the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
units.rightText: And the next sabbath almost the whole city was gathered together to hear the word of God.

units.leftText: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they blasphemously contradicted what Paul was saying.
units.rightText: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy, and contradicted the things which were spoken by Paul, and blasphemed.

units.leftText: Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: “It was necessary to speak the word of God to you first. But since you reject it and do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life, we now turn to the Gentiles.
units.rightText: And Paul and Barnabas spake out boldly, and said, It was necessary that the word of God should first be spoken to you. Seeing ye thrust it from you, and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, lo, we turn to the Gentiles.

units.leftText: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have made you a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’ ”
units.rightText: For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying, I have set thee for a light of the Gentiles, That thou shouldest be for salvation unto the uttermost part of the earth.

units.leftText: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed for eternal life believed.
units.rightText: And as the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of God: and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.

units.leftText: And the word of the Lord spread throughout that region.
units.rightText: And the word of the Lord was spread abroad throughout all the region.

units.leftText: The Jews, however, incited the religious women of prominence and the leading men of the city. They stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of their district.
units.rightText: But the Jews urged on the devout women of honorable estate, and the chief men of the city, and stirred up a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and cast them out of their borders.

units.leftText: So they shook the dust off their feet in protest against them and went to Iconium.
units.rightText: But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.

units.leftText: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue, where they spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
units.rightText: And it came to pass in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and so spake that a great multitude both of Jews and of Greeks believed.

units.leftText: But the unbelieving Jews stirred up the Gentiles and poisoned their minds against the brothers.
units.rightText: But the Jews that were disobedient stirred up the souls of the Gentiles, and made them evil affected against the brethren.

units.leftText: So Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time there, speaking boldly for the Lord, who affirmed the message of His grace by enabling them to perform signs and wonders.
units.rightText: Long time therefore they tarried there speaking boldly in the Lord, who bare witness unto the word of his grace, granting signs and wonders to be done by their hands.

units.leftText: The people of the city were divided. Some sided with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
units.rightText: But the multitude of the city was divided; and part held with the Jews, and part with the apostles.

units.leftText: But when the Gentiles and Jews, together with their rulers, set out to mistreat and stone them,
units.rightText: And when there was made an onset both of the Gentiles and of the Jews with their rulers, to treat them shamefully and to stone them,

units.leftText: they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding region,
units.rightText: they became aware of it, and fled unto the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and the region round about:

units.leftText: where they continued to preach the gospel. The Visit to Lystra and Derbe
units.rightText: and there they preached the gospel.

units.leftText: In Lystra there sat a man crippled in his feet, who was lame from birth and had never walked.
units.rightText: And at Lystra there sat a certain man, impotent in his feet, a cripple from his mother’s womb, who never had walked.

units.leftText: This man was listening to the words of Paul, who looked intently at him and saw that he had faith to be healed.
units.rightText: The same heard Paul speaking: who, fastening his eyes upon him, and seeing that he had faith to be made whole,

units.leftText: In a loud voice Paul called out, “Stand up on your feet!” And the man jumped up and began to walk.
units.rightText: said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. And he leaped up and walked.

units.leftText: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices in the Lycaonian language: “The gods have come down to us in human form!”
units.rightText: And when the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the speech of Lycaonia, The gods are come down to us in the likeness of men.

units.leftText: Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul they called Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
units.rightText: And they called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercury, because he was the chief speaker.

units.leftText: The priest of Zeus, whose temple was just outside the city, brought bulls and wreaths to the city gates, hoping to offer a sacrifice along with the crowds.
units.rightText: And the priest of Jupiter whose temple was before the city, brought oxen and garlands unto the gates, and would have done sacrifice with the multitudes.

units.leftText: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul found out about this, they tore their clothes and rushed into the crowd, shouting,
units.rightText: But when the apostles, Barnabas and Paul, heard of it, they rent their garments, and sprang forth among the multitude, crying out

units.leftText: “Men, why are you doing this? We too are only men, human like you. We are bringing you good news that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made heaven and earth and sea and everything in them.
units.rightText: and saying, Sirs, why do ye these things? We also are men of like passions with you, and bring you good tidings, that ye should turn from these vain things unto a living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea, and all that in them is:

units.leftText: In past generations, He let all nations go their own way.
units.rightText: who in the generations gone by suffered all the nations to walk in their own ways.

units.leftText: Yet He has not left Himself without testimony to His goodness: He gives you rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.”
units.rightText: And yet he left not himself without witness, in that he did good and gave you from heaven rains and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness.

units.leftText: Even with these words, Paul and Barnabas could hardly stop the crowds from sacrificing to them.
units.rightText: And with these sayings scarce restrained they the multitudes from doing sacrifice unto them.

units.leftText: Then some Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and won over the crowds. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, presuming he was dead.
units.rightText: But there came Jews thither from Antioch and Iconium: and having persuaded the multitudes, they stoned Paul, and dragged him out of the city, supposing that he was dead.

units.leftText: But after the disciples had gathered around him, he got up and went back into the city. And the next day he left with Barnabas for Derbe. Strengthening the Disciples
units.rightText: But as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up, and entered into the city: and on the morrow he went forth with Barnabas to Derbe.

units.leftText: They preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples. Then they returned to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
units.rightText: And when they had preached the gospel to that city, and had made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, and to Iconium, and to Antioch,

units.leftText: strengthening the souls of the disciples and encouraging them to continue in the faith. “We must endure many hardships to enter the kingdom of God,” they said.
units.rightText: confirming the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church, praying and fasting as they entrusted them to the Lord, in whom they had believed.
units.rightText: And when they had appointed for them elders in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord, on whom they had believed.

units.leftText: After passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
units.rightText: And they passed through Pisidia, and came to Pamphylia.

units.leftText: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
units.rightText: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia;

units.rightText: and thence they sailed to Antioch, from whence they had been committed to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.

units.leftText: When they arrived, they gathered the church together and reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
units.rightText: And when they were come, and had gathered the church together, they rehearsed all things that God had done with them, and that he had opened a door of faith unto the Gentiles.

units.leftText: And they spent a long time there with the disciples.

units.leftText: And after engaging these men in sharp debate, Paul and Barnabas were appointed, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem to see the apostles and elders about this question.
units.rightText: And when Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and questioning with them, the brethren appointed that Paul and Barnabas, and certain other of them, should go up to Jerusalem unto the apostles and elders about this question.

units.leftText: Sent on their way by the church, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting the conversion of the Gentiles and bringing great joy to all the brothers.
units.rightText: They therefore, being brought on their way by the church, passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, declaring the conversion of the Gentiles: and they caused great joy unto all the brethren.

units.leftText: On their arrival in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and apostles and elders, to whom they reported all that God had done through them. The Council at Jerusalem (Amos 9:11–15|AMO 9:11-15*; Galatians 2:1–10|GAL 2:1-10*)
units.rightText: And when they were come to Jerusalem, they were received of the church and the apostles and the elders, and they rehearsed all things that God had done with them.

units.leftText: But some believers from the party of the Pharisees stood up and declared, “The Gentiles must be circumcised and required to obey the law of Moses.”
units.rightText: But there rose up certain of the sect of the Pharisees who believed, saying, It is needful to circumcise them, and to charge them to keep the law of Moses.

units.leftText: So the apostles and elders met to look into this matter.
units.rightText: And the apostles and the elders were gathered together to consider of this matter.

units.leftText: After much discussion, Peter got up and said to them, “Brothers, you know that in the early days God made a choice among you that the Gentiles would hear from my lips the message of the gospel and believe.

units.leftText: And God, who knows the heart, showed His approval by giving the Holy Spirit to them, just as He did to us.

units.leftText: He made no distinction between us and them, for He cleansed their hearts by faith.

units.leftText: Now then, why do you test God by placing on the necks of the disciples a yoke that neither we nor our fathers have been able to bear?
units.rightText: Now therefore why make ye trial of God, that ye should put a yoke upon the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?

units.leftText: On the contrary, we believe it is through the grace of the Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.”
units.rightText: But we believe that we shall be saved through the grace of the Lord Jesus, in like manner as they.

units.leftText: The whole assembly fell silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul describing the signs and wonders God had done among the Gentiles through them.

units.rightText: But Paul and Barnabas tarried in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, with many others also.

units.leftText: As they went from town to town, they delivered the decisions handed down by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem for the people to obey.

units.leftText: From there we went to the Roman colony of Philippi, the leading city of that district of Macedonia. And we stayed there several days.

units.leftText: On the Sabbath we went outside the city gate along the river, where it was customary to find a place of prayer. After sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered there.
units.rightText: And on the sabbath day we went forth without the gate by a river side, where we supposed there was a place of prayer; and we sat down, and spake unto the women that were come together.

units.leftText: Among those listening was a woman named Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, who was a worshiper of God. The Lord opened her heart to respond to Paul’s message.
units.rightText: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, one that worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened to give heed unto the things which were spoken by Paul.

units.leftText: And when she and her household had been baptized, she urged us, “If you consider me a believer in the Lord, come and stay at my house.” And she persuaded us. Paul and Silas Imprisoned
units.rightText: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us.

units.leftText: One day as we were going to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl with a spirit of divination, who earned a large income for her masters by fortune-telling.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, as we were going to the place of prayer, that a certain maid having a spirit of divination met us, who brought her masters much gain by soothsaying.
leftNotes: 16:16 Greek a spirit of Python; that is, a spirit of divination named after the mythical serpent slain by Apollo

units.leftText: This girl followed Paul and the rest of us, shouting, “These men are servants of the Most High God, who are proclaiming to you the way of salvation!”
units.rightText: The same following after Paul and us cried out, saying, These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim unto you the way of salvation.

units.leftText: She continued this for many days. Eventually Paul grew so aggravated that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ I command you to come out of her!” And the spirit left her at that very moment.
units.rightText: And this she did for many days. But Paul, being sore troubled, turned and said to the spirit, I charge thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And it came out that very hour.

units.leftText: When the girl’s owners saw that their hope of making money was gone, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them before the authorities in the marketplace.
units.rightText: But when her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they laid hold on Paul and Silas, and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers,

units.rightText: and set forth customs which it is not lawful for us to receive, or to observe, being Romans.

units.leftText: The crowd joined in the attack against Paul and Silas, and the magistrates ordered that they be stripped and beaten with rods.
units.rightText: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent their garments off them, and commanded to beat them with rods.

units.leftText: And after striking them with many blows, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them securely.
units.rightText: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:

units.leftText: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the foundations of the prison. At once all the doors flew open and everyone’s chains came loose.
units.rightText: and suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison-house were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened; and every one’s bands were loosed.

units.leftText: When the jailer woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, presuming that the prisoners had escaped.
units.rightText: And the jailor, being roused out of sleep and seeing the prison doors open, drew his sword and was about to kill himself, supposing that the prisoners had escaped.

units.leftText: But Paul called out in a loud voice, “Do not harm yourself! We are all here!”
units.rightText: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.

units.leftText: Calling for lights, the jailer rushed in and fell trembling before Paul and Silas.

units.rightText: and brought them out and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

units.rightText: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus, and thou shalt be saved, thou and thy house.

units.leftText: Then Paul and Silas spoke the word of the Lord to him and to everyone in his house.
units.rightText: And they spake the word of the Lord unto him, with all that were in his house.

units.leftText: At that hour of the night, the jailer took them and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized.
units.rightText: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, immediately.

units.leftText: Then he brought them into his home and set a meal before them. So he and all his household rejoiced that they had come to believe in God. An Official Apology
units.rightText: And he brought them up into his house, and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly, with all his house, having believed in God.

units.leftText: When daylight came, the magistrates sent their officers with the order: “Release those men.”
units.rightText: But when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.

units.leftText: The jailer informed Paul: “The magistrates have sent orders to release you. Now you may go on your way in peace.”
units.rightText: And the jailor reported the words to Paul, saying, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore come forth, and go in peace.

units.leftText: But Paul said to the officers, “They beat us publicly without a trial and threw us into prison, even though we are Roman citizens. And now do they want to send us away secretly? Absolutely not! Let them come themselves and escort us out!”
units.rightText: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us publicly, uncondemned, men that are Romans, and have cast us into prison; and do they now cast us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and bring us out.

units.leftText: So the officers relayed this message to the magistrates, who were alarmed to hear that Paul and Silas were Roman citizens.
units.rightText: And the serjeants reported these words unto the magistrates: and they feared when they heard that they were Romans;

units.leftText: They came to appease them and led them out, requesting that they leave the city.
units.rightText: and they came and besought them; and when they had brought them out, they asked them to go away from the city.

units.leftText: After Paul and Silas came out of the prison, they went to Lydia’s house to see the brothers and encourage them. Then they left the city.
units.rightText: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.

units.leftText: When they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue.

units.leftText: As was his custom, Paul went into the synagogue, and on three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
units.rightText: and Paul, as his custom was, went in unto them, and for three sabbath days reasoned with them from the scriptures,

units.rightText: opening and alleging that it behooved the Christ to suffer, and to rise again from the dead; and that this Jesus, whom, said he, I proclaim unto you, is the Christ.

units.leftText: Some of the Jews were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a large number of God-fearing Greeks and quite a few leading women.
units.rightText: And some of them were persuaded, and consorted with Paul and Silas; and of the devout Greeks a great multitude, and of the chief women not a few.

units.leftText: The Jews, however, became jealous. So they brought in some troublemakers from the marketplace, formed a mob, and sent the city into an uproar. They raided Jason’s house in search of Paul and Silas, hoping to bring them out to the people.
units.rightText: But the Jews, being moved with jealousy, took unto them certain vile fellows of the rabble, and gathering a crowd, set the city on an uproar; and assaulting the house of Jason, they sought to bring them forth to the people.

units.leftText: But when they could not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city officials, shouting, “These men who have turned the world upside down have now come here,
units.rightText: And when they found them not, they dragged Jason and certain brethren before the rulers of the city, crying, These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also;

units.leftText: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. They are all defying Caesar’s decrees, saying that there is another king, named Jesus!”
units.rightText: whom Jason hath received: and these all act contrary to the decrees of Cæsar, saying that there is another king, one Jesus.

units.leftText: On hearing this, the crowd and city officials were greatly disturbed.
units.rightText: And they troubled the multitude and the rulers of the city, when they heard these things.

units.leftText: And they collected bond from Jason and the others and then released them. The Character of the Bereans
units.rightText: And when they had taken security from Jason and the rest, they let them go.

units.leftText: As soon as night had fallen, the brothers sent Paul and Silas away to Berea. On arriving there, they went into the Jewish synagogue.
units.rightText: And the brethren immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night unto Beroea: who when they were come thither went into the synagogue of the Jews.

units.leftText: Now the Bereans were more noble-minded than the Thessalonians, for they received the message with great eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if these teachings were true.
units.rightText: Now these were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, examining the scriptures daily, whether these things were so.
leftNotes: 17:11 Literally with great eagerness, every day examining the Writings, whether these things were so.

units.leftText: As a result, many of them believed, along with quite a few prominent Greek women and men.
units.rightText: Many of them therefore believed; also of the Greek women of honorable estate, and of men, not a few.

units.leftText: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that Paul was also proclaiming the word of God in Berea, they went there themselves to incite and agitate the crowds.
units.rightText: But when the Jews of Thessalonica had knowledge that the word of God was proclaimed of Paul at Beroea also, they came thither likewise, stirring up and troubling the multitudes.

units.leftText: The brothers immediately sent Paul to the coast, but Silas and Timothy remained in Berea.
units.rightText: And then immediately the brethren sent forth Paul to go as far as to the sea: and Silas and Timothy abode there still.

units.leftText: Those who escorted Paul brought him to Athens and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
units.rightText: But they that conducted Paul brought him as far as Athens: and receiving a commandment unto Silas and Timothy that they should come to him with all speed, they departed.

units.leftText: While Paul was waiting for them in Athens, he was deeply disturbed in his spirit to see that the city was full of idols.
units.rightText: Now while Paul waited for them at Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he beheld the city full of idols.

units.leftText: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles, and in the marketplace with those he met each day.
units.rightText: So he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and the devout persons, and in the marketplace every day with them that met him.

units.leftText: Some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also began to debate with him. Some of them asked, “What is this babbler trying to say?” Others said, “He seems to be advocating foreign gods.” They said this because Paul was proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection.
units.rightText: And certain also of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers encountered him. And some said, What would this babbler say? others, He seemeth to be a setter forth of strange gods: because he preached Jesus and the resurrection.

units.leftText: So they took Paul and brought him to the Areopagus, where they asked him, “May we know what this new teaching is that you are presenting?
