units.leftText: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.
units.rightText: And Paul, having tarried after this yet many days, took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence for Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila: having shorn his head in Cenchreæ; for he had a vow.

units.leftText: When they reached Ephesus, Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.
units.rightText: And they came to Ephesus, and he left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.

units.leftText: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.
units.rightText: And when they asked him to abide a longer time, he consented not;

units.leftText: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.
units.rightText: but taking his leave of them, and saying, I will return again unto you if God will, he set sail from Ephesus.
leftNotes: 18:21 BYZ and TR I must by all means keep this feast that comes in Jerusalem, but I will come back

units.leftText: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch. Paul’s Third Missionary Journey Begins (Acts 13:1–3|ACT 13:1-3*; Acts 15:36–41|ACT 15:36-41*)
units.rightText: And when he had landed at Cæsarea, he went up and saluted the church, and went down to Antioch.
leftNotes: 18:22 Literally he went up and greeted the church

units.leftText: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.
units.rightText: And having spent some time there, he departed, and went through the region of Galatia, and Phrygia, in order, establishing all the disciples.

units.leftText: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.
units.rightText: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by race, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus; and he was mighty in the scriptures.

units.leftText: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
units.rightText: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spake and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John:
leftNotes: 18:25 BYZ and TR about the Lord

units.leftText: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
units.rightText: and he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more accurately.

units.leftText: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.
units.rightText: And when he was minded to pass over into Achaia, the brethren encouraged him, and wrote to the disciples to receive him: and when he was come, he helped them much that had believed through grace;

units.leftText: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
units.rightText: for he powerfully confuted the Jews, and that publicly, showing by the scriptures that Jesus was the Christ.

units.leftText: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the interior and came to Ephesus. There he found some disciples
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper country came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples:
leftNotes: 19:1 Or the highland

units.leftText: and asked them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you became believers?” “No,” they answered, “we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”
units.rightText: and he said unto them, Did ye receive the Holy Spirit when ye believed? And they said unto him, Nay, we did not so much as hear whether the Holy Spirit was given.

units.leftText: “Into what, then, were you baptized?” Paul asked. “The baptism of John,” they replied.
units.rightText: And he said, Into what then were ye baptized? And they said, Into John’s baptism.

units.leftText: Paul explained: “John’s baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus.”
units.rightText: And Paul said, John baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying unto the people that they should believe on him that should come after him, that is, on Jesus.

units.leftText: On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: And when they heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.

units.leftText: And when Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
units.rightText: And when Paul had laid his hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came on them; and they spake with tongues, and prophesied.

units.leftText: There were about twelve men in all. Paul Ministers in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1–2|EPH 1:1-2*; Revelation 2:1–7|REV 2:1-7*)
units.rightText: And they were in all about twelve men.

units.leftText: Then Paul went into the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.
units.rightText: And he entered into the synagogue, and spake boldly for the space of three months, reasoning and persuading as to the things concerning the kingdom of God.

units.leftText: But when some of them stubbornly refused to believe and publicly maligned the Way, Paul took his disciples and left the synagogue to conduct daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
units.rightText: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.

units.leftText: This continued for two years, so that everyone who lived in the province of Asia, Jews and Greeks alike, heard the word of the Lord.
units.rightText: And this continued for the space of two years; so that all they that dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord, both Jews and Greeks.
leftNotes: 19:10 Literally in Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey; similarly in verses 22, 26, 27, and 31.

units.leftText: God did extraordinary miracles through the hands of Paul,
units.rightText: And God wrought special miracles by the hands of Paul:

units.leftText: so that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and the diseases and evil spirits left them. Seven Sons of Sceva
units.rightText: insomuch that unto the sick were carried away from his body handkerchiefs or aprons, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
leftNotes: 19:12 Greek soudaria

units.leftText: Now there were some itinerant Jewish exorcists who tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those with evil spirits. They would say, “I command you by Jesus, whom Paul proclaims.”
units.rightText: But certain also of the strolling Jews, exorcists, took upon them to name over them that had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, I adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preacheth.

units.leftText: Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
units.rightText: And there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jew, a chief priest, who did this.

units.leftText: But one day the evil spirit responded, “Jesus I know, and I know about Paul, but who are you?”
units.rightText: And the evil spirit answered and said unto them, Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are ye?

units.leftText: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.
units.rightText: And the man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, and mastered both of them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

units.leftText: This became known to all the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, and fear came over all of them. So the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
units.rightText: And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, that dwelt at Ephesus; and fear fell upon them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

units.leftText: Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.
units.rightText: Many also of them that had believed came, confessing, and declaring their deeds.

units.leftText: And a number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books and burned them in front of everyone. When the value of the books was calculated, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.
units.rightText: And not a few of them that practised magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all; and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.
leftNotes: 19:19 Or fifty thousand pieces of silver. A drachma was a silver coin worth about one day’s wages.

units.leftText: So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail. The Riot in Ephesus
units.rightText: So mightily grew the word of the Lord and prevailed.

units.leftText: After these things had happened, Paul resolved in the Spirit to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. “After I have been there,” he said, “I must see Rome as well.”
units.rightText: Now after these things were ended, Paul purposed in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, After I have been there, I must also see Rome.
leftNotes: 19:21 Or resolved in spirit

units.leftText: He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed for a time in the province of Asia.
units.rightText: And having sent into Macedonia two of them that ministered unto him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.

units.leftText: About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.
units.rightText: And about that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.
leftNotes: 19:23 Literally there arose no little disturbance

units.leftText: It began with a silversmith named Demetrius who made silver shrines of Artemis, bringing much business to the craftsmen.
units.rightText: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Diana, brought no little business unto the craftsmen;
leftNotes: 19:24 Literally bringing no little business

units.leftText: Demetrius assembled the craftsmen, along with the workmen in related trades. “Men,” he said, “you know that this business is our source of prosperity.
units.rightText: whom he gathered together, with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this business we have our wealth.

units.leftText: And you can see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but in nearly the whole province of Asia, this Paul has persuaded a great number of people to turn away. He says that man-made gods are no gods at all.
units.rightText: And ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they are no gods, that are made with hands:

units.leftText: There is danger not only that our business will fall into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited and her majesty deposed — she who is worshiped by all the province of Asia and the whole world.”
units.rightText: and not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana be made of no account, and that she should even be deposed from her magnificence whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.

units.leftText: When the men heard this, they were enraged and began shouting, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
units.rightText: And when they heard this they were filled with wrath, and cried out, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

units.leftText: Soon the whole city was in disarray. They rushed together into the theatre, dragging with them Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul’s traveling companions from Macedonia.
units.rightText: And the city was filled with the confusion: and they rushed with one accord into the theatre, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.

units.leftText: Paul wanted to go before the assembly, but the disciples would not allow him.
units.rightText: And when Paul was minded to enter in unto the people, the disciples suffered him not.

units.leftText: Even some of Paul’s friends who were officials of the province of Asia sent word to him, begging him not to venture into the theatre.
units.rightText: And certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent unto him and besought him not to adventure himself into the theatre.
leftNotes: 19:31 Or friends who were Asiarchs

units.leftText: Meanwhile the assembly was in turmoil. Some were shouting one thing and some another, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
units.rightText: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another: for the assembly was in confusion; and the more part knew not wherefore they were come together.

units.leftText: The Jews in the crowd pushed Alexander forward to explain himself, and he motioned for silence so he could make his defense to the people.
units.rightText: And they brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made a defence unto the people.

units.leftText: But when they realized that he was a Jew, they all shouted in unison for about two hours: “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”
units.rightText: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.

units.leftText: Finally the city clerk quieted the crowd and declared, “Men of Ephesus, doesn’t everyone know that the city of Ephesus is guardian of the temple of the great Artemis and of her image, which fell from heaven?
units.rightText: And when the townclerk had quieted the multitude, he saith, Ye men of Ephesus, what man is there who knoweth not that the city of the Ephesians is temple-keeper of the great Diana, and of the image which fell down from Jupiter?

units.leftText: Since these things are undeniable, you ought to be calm and not do anything rash.
units.rightText: Seeing then that these things cannot be gainsaid, ye ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.

units.leftText: For you have brought these men here, though they have neither robbed our temple nor blasphemed our goddess.
units.rightText: For ye have brought hither these men, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of our goddess.

units.leftText: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.
units.rightText: If therefore Demetrius, and the craftsmen that are with him, have a matter against any man, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls: let them accuse one another.

units.leftText: But if you are seeking anything beyond this, it must be settled in a legal assembly.
units.rightText: But if ye seek anything about other matters, it shall be settled in the regular assembly.

units.leftText: For we are in jeopardy of being charged with rioting for today’s events, and we have no justification to account for this commotion.”
units.rightText: For indeed we are in danger to be accused concerning this day’s riot, there being no cause for it: and as touching it we shall not be able to give account of this concourse.

units.leftText: After he had said this, he dismissed the assembly.
units.rightText: And when he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.

units.leftText: When the uproar had ended, Paul sent for the disciples. And after encouraging them, he said goodbye to them and left for Macedonia.
units.rightText: And after the uproar ceased, Paul having sent for the disciples and exhorted them, took leave of them, and departed to go into Macedonia.

units.leftText: After traveling through that area and speaking many words of encouragement, he arrived in Greece,
units.rightText: And when he had gone through those parts, and had given them much exhortation, he came into Greece.

units.leftText: where he stayed three months. And when the Jews formed a plot against him as he was about to sail for Syria, he decided to go back through Macedonia.
units.rightText: And when he had spent three months there, and a plot was laid against him by the Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he determined to return through Macedonia.

units.leftText: Paul was accompanied by Sopater son of Pyrrhus from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from the province of Asia.
units.rightText: And there accompanied him as far as Asia, Sopater of Beroea, the son of Pyrrhus; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
leftNotes: 20:4 Literally from Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey; also in verses 16 and 18.

units.leftText: These men went on ahead and waited for us in Troas.
units.rightText: But these had gone before, and were waiting for us at Troas.

units.leftText: And after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi, and five days later we rejoined them in Troas, where we stayed seven days. Eutychus Revived at Troas (2 Kings 4:18–37|2KI 4:18-37*)
units.rightText: And we sailed away from Philippi after the days of unleavened bread, and came unto them to Troas in five days; where we tarried seven days.
leftNotes: 20:6 Literally after the days of the Unleavened; see Exodus 12:14–20|EXO 12:14-20*.

units.leftText: On the first day of the week we came together to break bread. Since Paul was ready to leave the next day, he talked to them and kept on speaking until midnight.
units.rightText: And upon the first day of the week, when we were gathered together to break bread, Paul discoursed with them, intending to depart on the morrow; and prolonged his speech until midnight.

units.leftText: Now there were many lamps in the upper room where we were gathered.
units.rightText: And there were many lights in the upper chamber where we were gathered together.

units.leftText: And a certain young man named Eutychus, seated in the window, was sinking into a deep sleep as Paul talked on and on. When he was sound asleep, he fell from the third story and was picked up dead.
units.rightText: And there sat in the window a certain young man named Eutychus, borne down with deep sleep; and as Paul discoursed yet longer, being borne down by his sleep he fell down from the third story, and was taken up dead.

units.leftText: But Paul went down, threw himself on the young man, and embraced him. “Do not be alarmed!” he said. “He is still alive!”
units.rightText: And Paul went down, and fell on him, and embracing him said, Make ye no ado; for his life is in him.

units.leftText: Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread, and ate. And after speaking until daybreak, he departed.
units.rightText: And when he was gone up, and had broken the bread, and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even till break of day, so he departed.

units.leftText: And the people were greatly relieved to take the boy home alive. From Troas to Miletus
units.rightText: And they brought the lad alive, and were not a little comforted.

units.leftText: We went on ahead to the ship and sailed to Assos, where we were to take Paul aboard. He had arranged this because he was going there on foot.
units.rightText: But we, going before to the ship, set sail for Assos, there intending to take in Paul: for so had he appointed, intending himself to go by land.

units.leftText: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and went on to Mitylene.
units.rightText: And when he met us at Assos, we took him in, and came to Mitylene.

units.leftText: Sailing on from there, we arrived the next day opposite Chios. The day after that we arrived at Samos, and on the following day we came to Miletus.
units.rightText: And sailing from thence, we came the following day over against Chios; and the next day we touched at Samos; and the day after we came to Miletus.
leftNotes: 20:15 BYZ and TR and, after remaining at Trogyllium,

units.leftText: Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus to avoid spending time in the province of Asia, because he was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if possible, by the day of Pentecost. Paul’s Farewell to the Ephesians
units.rightText: For Paul had determined to sail past Ephesus, that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem the day of Pentecost.
leftNotes: 20:16 That is, Shavuot, the late spring feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; it is also known as the Feast of Harvest(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16*) or the Feast of Weeks(see Exodus 34:22|EXO 34:22*).

units.leftText: From Miletus, Paul sent to Ephesus for the elders of the church.
units.rightText: And from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called to him the elders of the church.

units.leftText: When they came to him, he said, “You know how I lived the whole time I was with you, from the first day I arrived in the province of Asia.
units.rightText: And when they were come to him, he said unto them, Ye yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, after what manner I was with you all the time,

units.leftText: I served the Lord with great humility and with tears, especially in the trials that came upon me through the plots of the Jews.
units.rightText: serving the Lord with all lowliness of mind, and with tears, and with trials which befell me by the plots of the Jews;

units.leftText: I did not shrink back from declaring anything that was helpful to you as I taught you publicly and from house to house,
units.rightText: how I shrank not from declaring unto you anything that was profitable, and teaching you publicly, and from house to house,

units.leftText: testifying to Jews and Greeks alike about repentance to God and faith in our Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: testifying both to Jews and to Greeks repentance toward God, and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
leftNotes: 20:21 ECM, TR, and Tischendorf; SBL, NE, BYZ, and WH our Lord Jesus

units.leftText: And now, compelled by the Spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing what will happen to me there.
units.rightText: And now, behold, I go bound in the spirit unto Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall befall me there:

units.leftText: I only know that in town after town the Holy Spirit warns me that chains and afflictions await me.
units.rightText: save that the Holy Spirit testifieth unto me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions abide me.

units.leftText: But I consider my life of no value to me, if only I may finish my course and complete the ministry I have received from the Lord Jesus — the ministry of testifying to the good news of God’s grace.
units.rightText: But I hold not my life of any account as dear unto myself, so that I may accomplish my course, and the ministry which I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God.

units.leftText: Now I know that none of you among whom I have preached the kingdom will see my face again.
units.rightText: And now, behold, I know that ye all, among whom I went about preaching the kingdom, shall see my face no more.

units.leftText: Therefore I testify to you this day that I am innocent of the blood of all men.
units.rightText: Wherefore I testify unto you this day, that I am pure from the blood of all men.

units.leftText: For I did not shrink back from declaring to you the whole will of God.
units.rightText: For I shrank not from declaring unto you the whole counsel of God.

units.leftText: Keep watch over yourselves and the entire flock of which the Holy Spirit has made you overseers. Be shepherds of the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
units.rightText: Take heed unto yourselves, and to all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit hath made you bishops, to feed the church of the Lord which he purchased with his own blood.
leftNotes: 20:28 Tischendorf of the Lord; BYZ and PT of the Lord and God
20:28 Or with the blood of His own Son.

units.leftText: I know that after my departure, savage wolves will come in among you and will not spare the flock.
units.rightText: I know that after my departing grievous wolves shall enter in among you, not sparing the flock;

units.leftText: Even from your own number, men will rise up and distort the truth to draw away disciples after them.
units.rightText: and from among your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after them.

units.leftText: Therefore be alert and remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you night and day with tears.
units.rightText: Wherefore watch ye, remembering that by the space of three years I ceased not to admonish every one night and day with tears.

units.leftText: And now I commit you to God and to the word of His grace, which can build you up and give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
units.rightText: And now I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you the inheritance among all them that are sanctified.

units.leftText: I have not coveted anyone’s silver or gold or clothing.
units.rightText: I coveted no man’s silver, or gold, or apparel.

units.leftText: You yourselves know that these hands of mine have ministered to my own needs and those of my companions.
units.rightText: Ye yourselves know that these hands ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.

units.leftText: In everything, I showed you that by this kind of hard work we must help the weak, remembering the words of the Lord Jesus Himself: ‘It is more blessed to give than to receive.’”
units.rightText: In all things I gave you an example, that so laboring ye ought to help the weak, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he himself said, It is more blessed to give than to receive.

units.leftText: When Paul had said this, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
units.rightText: And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down and prayed with them all.

units.leftText: They all wept openly as they embraced Paul and kissed him.
units.rightText: And they all wept sore, and fell on Paul’s neck and kissed him,

units.leftText: They were especially grieved by his statement that they would never see his face again. Then they accompanied him to the ship.
units.rightText: sorrowing most of all for the word which he had spoken, that they should behold his face no more. And they brought him on his way unto the ship.

units.leftText: After we had torn ourselves away from them, we sailed directly to Cos, and the next day on to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
units.rightText: And when it came to pass that we were parted from them and had set sail, we came with a straight course unto Cos, and the next day unto Rhodes, and from thence unto Patara:

units.leftText: Finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we boarded it and set sail.
units.rightText: and having found a ship crossing over unto Phoenicia, we went aboard, and set sail.

units.leftText: After sighting Cyprus and passing south of it, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, where the ship was to unload its cargo.
units.rightText: And when we had come in sight of Cyprus, leaving it on the left hand, we sailed unto Syria, and landed at Tyre; for there the ship was to unlade her burden.

units.leftText: We sought out the disciples in Tyre and stayed with them seven days. Through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And having found the disciples, we tarried there seven days: and these said to Paul through the Spirit, that he should not set foot in Jerusalem.

units.leftText: But when our time there had ended, we set out on our journey. All the disciples, with their wives and children, accompanied us out of the city and knelt down on the beach to pray with us.
units.rightText: And when it came to pass that we had accomplished the days, we departed and went on our journey; and they all, with wives and children, brought us on our way till we were out of the city: and kneeling down on the beach, we prayed, and bade each other farewell;

units.leftText: And after we had said our farewells, we went aboard the ship, and they returned home.
units.rightText: and we went on board the ship, but they returned home again.

units.leftText: When we had finished our voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and stayed with them for a day. Paul Visits Philip the Evangelist
units.rightText: And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais; and we saluted the brethren, and abode with them one day.

units.leftText: Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea and stayed at the home of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the Seven.
units.rightText: And on the morrow we departed, and came unto Cæsarea: and entering into the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we abode with him.
leftNotes: 21:8 See Acts 6:5|ACT 6:5*.

units.leftText: He had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
units.rightText: Now this man had four virgin daughters, who prophesied.

units.leftText: After we had been there several days, a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
units.rightText: And as we tarried there some days, there came down from Judæa a certain prophet, named Agabus.

units.leftText: Coming over to us, he took Paul’s belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, “The Holy Spirit says: ‘In this way the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the Gentiles.’”
units.rightText: And coming to us, and taking Paul’s girdle, he bound his own feet and hands, and said, Thus saith the Holy Spirit, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.

units.leftText: When we heard this, we and the people there pleaded with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And when we heard these things, both we and they of that place besought him not to go up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Then Paul answered, “Why are you weeping and breaking my heart? I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.”
units.rightText: Then Paul answered, What do ye, weeping and breaking my heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.

units.leftText: When he would not be dissuaded, we quieted down and said, “The Lord’s will be done.”
units.rightText: And when he would not be persuaded, we ceased, saying, The will of the Lord be done.

units.leftText: After these days, we packed up and went on to Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And after these days we took up our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Some of the disciples from Caesarea accompanied us, and they took us to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple. Paul’s Arrival at Jerusalem
units.rightText: And there went with us also certain of the disciples from Cæsarea, bringing with them one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we should lodge.

units.leftText: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the brothers welcomed us joyfully.
units.rightText: And when we were come to Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.

units.leftText: The next day Paul went in with us to see James, and all the elders were present.
units.rightText: And the day following Paul went in with us unto James; and all the elders were present.

units.leftText: Paul greeted them and recounted one by one the things that God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
units.rightText: And when he had saluted them, he rehearsed one by one the things which God had wrought among the Gentiles through his ministry.

units.leftText: When they heard this, they glorified God. Then they said to Paul, “You see, brother, how many thousands of Jews have believed, and all of them are zealous for the law.
units.rightText: And they, when they heard it, glorified God; and they said unto him, Thou seest, brother, how many thousands there are among the Jews of them that have believed; and they are all zealous for the law:

units.leftText: But they are under the impression that you teach all the Jews who live among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or observe our customs.
units.rightText: and they have been informed concerning thee, that thou teachest all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children, neither to walk after the customs.

units.leftText: What then should we do? They will certainly hear that you have come.
units.rightText: What is it therefore? they will certainly hear that thou art come.

units.leftText: Therefore do what we advise you. There are four men with us who have taken a vow.
units.rightText: Do therefore this that we say to thee: We have four men that have a vow on them;

units.leftText: Take these men, purify yourself along with them, and pay their expenses so they can have their heads shaved. Then everyone will know that there is no truth to these rumors about you, but that you also live in obedience to the law.
units.rightText: these take, and purify thyself with them, and be at charges for them, that they may shave their heads: and all shall know that there is no truth in the things whereof they have been informed concerning thee; but that thou thyself also walkest orderly, keeping the law.

units.leftText: As for the Gentile believers, we have written to them our decision that they must abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality.”
units.rightText: But as touching the Gentiles that have believed, we wrote, giving judgment that they should keep themselves from things sacrificed to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from fornication.

units.leftText: So the next day Paul took the men and purified himself along with them. Then he entered the temple to give notice of the date when their purification would be complete and the offering would be made for each of them. Paul Seized at the Temple
units.rightText: Then Paul took the men, and the next day purifying himself with them went into the temple, declaring the fulfilment of the days of purification, until the offering was offered for every one of them.

units.leftText: When the seven days were almost over, some Jews from the province of Asia saw Paul at the temple. They stirred up the whole crowd and seized him,
units.rightText: And when the seven days were almost completed, the Jews from Asia, when they saw him in the temple, stirred up all the multitude and laid hands on him,
leftNotes: 21:27 Literally from Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey.

units.leftText: crying out, “Men of Israel, help us! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against our people and against our law and against this place. Furthermore, he has brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.”
units.rightText: crying out, Men of Israel, help: This is the man that teacheth all men everywhere against the people, and the law, and this place; and moreover he brought Greeks also into the temple, and hath defiled this holy place.

units.leftText: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they assumed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
units.rightText: For they had before seen with him in the city Trophimus the Ephesian, whom they supposed that Paul had brought into the temple.

units.leftText: The whole city was stirred up, and the people rushed together. They seized Paul and dragged him out of the temple, and at once the gates were shut.
units.rightText: And all the city was moved, and the people ran together; and they laid hold on Paul, and dragged him out of the temple: and straightway the doors were shut.

units.leftText: While they were trying to kill him, the commander of the Roman regiment received a report that all Jerusalem was in turmoil.
units.rightText: And as they were seeking to kill him, tidings came up to the chief captain of the band, that all Jerusalem was in confusion.
leftNotes: 21:31 Literally the commander of the cohort

units.leftText: Immediately he took some soldiers and centurions and ran down to the crowd. When the people saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
units.rightText: And forthwith he took soldiers and centurions, and ran down upon them: and they, when they saw the chief captain and the soldiers, left off beating Paul.

units.leftText: The commander came up and arrested Paul, ordering that he be bound with two chains. Then he asked who he was and what he had done.
units.rightText: Then the chief captain came near, and laid hold on him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and inquired who he was, and what he had done.

units.leftText: Some in the crowd were shouting one thing, and some another. And since the commander could not get at the truth because of the uproar, he ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks.
units.rightText: And some shouted one thing, some another, among the crowd: and when he could not know the certainty for the uproar, he commanded him to be brought into the castle.

units.leftText: When Paul reached the steps, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the mob.
units.rightText: And when he came upon the stairs, so it was that he was borne of the soldiers for the violence of the crowd;

units.leftText: For the crowd that followed him kept shouting, “Away with him!” Paul Addresses the Crowd
units.rightText: for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, Away with him.

units.leftText: As they were about to take Paul into the barracks, he asked the commander, “May I say something to you?”
units.rightText: And as Paul was about to be brought into the castle, he saith unto the chief captain, May I say something unto thee? And he said, Dost thou know Greek?

units.leftText: “Aren’t you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the Assassins into the wilderness?”
units.rightText: Art thou not then the Egyptian, who before these days stirred up to sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the Assassins?

units.leftText: But Paul answered, “I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city. Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people.”
units.rightText: But Paul said, I am a Jew, of Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no mean city: and I beseech thee, give me leave to speak unto the people.

units.leftText: Having received permission, Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the crowd. A great hush came over the crowd, and he addressed them in Hebrew:
units.rightText: And when he had given him leave, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with the hand unto the people; and when there was made a great silence, he spake unto them in the Hebrew language, saying,
leftNotes: 21:40 Or in Aramaic; literally in the Hebrew language

units.leftText: “Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.”
units.rightText: Brethren and fathers, hear ye the defence which I now make unto you.

units.leftText: When they heard him speak to them in Hebrew, they became even more quiet.
units.rightText: And when they heard that he spake unto them in the Hebrew language, they were the more quiet: and he saith,
leftNotes: 22:2 Or in Aramaic; literally in the Hebrew language

units.leftText: “I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but raised in this city. I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers. I was just as zealous for God as any of you are today.
units.rightText: I am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel, instructed according to the strict manner of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God, even as ye all are this day:

units.leftText: I persecuted this Way even to the death, detaining both men and women and throwing them into prison,
units.rightText: and I persecuted this Way unto the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women.

units.leftText: as the high priest and the whole Council can testify about me. I even obtained letters from them to their brothers in Damascus, and I was on my way to apprehend these people and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
units.rightText: As also the high priest doth bear me witness, and all the estate of the elders: from whom also I received letters unto the brethren, and journeyed to Damascus to bring them also that were there unto Jerusalem in bonds to be punished.

units.leftText: About noon as I was approaching Damascus, suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, as I made my journey, and drew nigh unto Damascus, about noon, suddenly there shone from heaven a great light round about me.

units.leftText: I fell to the ground and heard a voice say to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?’
units.rightText: And I fell unto the ground, and heard a voice saying unto me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

units.leftText: ‘Who are You, Lord?’ I asked.
units.rightText: And I answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said unto me, I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom thou persecutest.

units.leftText: My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me.
units.rightText: And they that were with me beheld indeed the light, but they heard not the voice of him that spake to me.

units.leftText: Then I asked, ‘What should I do, Lord?’ ‘Get up and go into Damascus,’ He told me. ‘There you will be told all that you have been appointed to do.’
units.rightText: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise, and go into Damascus; and there it shall be told thee of all things which are appointed for thee to do.

units.leftText: Because the brilliance of the light had blinded me, my companions led me by the hand into Damascus.
units.rightText: And when I could not see for the glory of that light, being led by the hand of them that were with me I came into Damascus.

units.leftText: There a man named Ananias, a devout observer of the law who was highly regarded by all the Jews living there,
units.rightText: And one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well reported of by all the Jews that dwelt there,

units.leftText: came and stood beside me. ‘Brother Saul,’ he said, ‘receive your sight.’ And at that moment I could see him.
units.rightText: came unto me, and standing by me said unto me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And in that very hour I looked up on him.

units.leftText: Then he said, ‘The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will and to see the Righteous One and to hear His voice.
units.rightText: And he said, The God of our fathers hath appointed thee to know his will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from his mouth.

units.leftText: You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard.
units.rightText: For thou shalt be a witness for him unto all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

units.leftText: And now what are you waiting for? Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name.’
units.rightText: And now why tarriest thou? arise, and be baptized, and wash away thy sins, calling on his name.

units.leftText: Later, when I had returned to Jerusalem and was praying at the temple, I fell into a trance
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that, when I had returned to Jerusalem, and while I prayed in the temple, I fell into a trance,

units.leftText: and saw the Lord saying to me, ‘Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me.’
units.rightText: and saw him saying unto me, Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem; because they will not receive of thee testimony concerning me.
leftNotes: 22:18 Literally saw Him

units.leftText: ‘Lord,’ I answered, ‘they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.
units.rightText: And I said, Lord, they themselves know that I imprisoned and beat in every synagogue them that believed on thee:

units.leftText: And when the blood of Your witness Stephen was shed, I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him.’
units.rightText: and when the blood of Stephen thy witness was shed, I also was standing by, and consenting, and keeping the garments of them that slew him.
leftNotes: 22:20 Or martyr

units.leftText: Then He said to me, ‘Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles.’” Paul the Roman Citizen
units.rightText: And he said unto me, Depart: for I will send thee forth far hence unto the Gentiles.

units.leftText: The crowd listened to Paul until he made this statement. Then they lifted up their voices and shouted, “Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!”
units.rightText: And they gave him audience unto this word; and they lifted up their voice, and said, Away with such a fellow from the earth: for it is not fit that he should live.

units.leftText: As they were shouting and throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air,
units.rightText: And as they cried out, and threw off their garments, and cast dust into the air,

units.leftText: the commander ordered that Paul be brought into the barracks. He directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated to determine the reason for this outcry against him.
units.rightText: the chief captain commanded him to be brought into the castle, bidding that he should be examined by scourging, that he might know for what cause they so shouted against him.

units.leftText: But as they stretched him out to strap him down, Paul said to the centurion standing there, “Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?”
units.rightText: And when they had tied him up with the thongs, Paul said unto the centurion that stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man that is a Roman, and uncondemned?

units.leftText: On hearing this, the centurion went and reported it to the commander. “What are you going to do?” he said. “This man is a Roman citizen.”
units.rightText: And when the centurion heard it, he went to the chief captain and told him, saying, What art thou about to do? for this man is a Roman.

units.leftText: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” he answered.
units.rightText: And the chief captain came and said unto him, Tell me, art thou a Roman? And he said, Yea.

units.leftText: “I paid a high price for my citizenship,” said the commander. “But I was born a citizen,” Paul replied.
units.rightText: And the chief captain answered, With a great sum obtained I this citizenship. And Paul said, But I am a Roman born.

units.leftText: At once those who were about to interrogate Paul stepped back, and the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains.
units.rightText: They then that were about to examine him straightway departed from him: and the chief captain also was afraid when he knew that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

units.leftText: The next day the commander, wanting to learn the real reason Paul was accused by the Jews, released him and ordered the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrin to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and had him stand before them.
units.rightText: But on the morrow, desiring to know the certainty wherefore he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to come together, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
leftNotes: 22:30 Or the whole Council

units.leftText: Paul looked directly at the Sanhedrin and said, “Brothers, I have conducted myself before God in all good conscience to this day.”
units.rightText: And Paul, looking stedfastly on the council, said, Brethren, I have lived before God in all good conscience until this day.
leftNotes: 23:1 Or the Council; also in verses 6, 15, 20, and 28

units.leftText: At this, the high priest Ananias ordered those standing near Paul to strike him on the mouth.
units.rightText: And the high priest Ananias commanded them that stood by him to smite him on the mouth.

units.leftText: Then Paul said to him, “God will strike you, you whitewashed wall! You sit here to judge me according to the law, yet you yourself violate the law by commanding that I be struck.”
units.rightText: Then said Paul unto him, God shall smite thee, thou whited wall: and sittest thou to judge me according to the law, and commandest me to be smitten contrary to the law?

units.leftText: But those standing nearby said, “How dare you insult the high priest of God!”
units.rightText: And they that stood by said, Revilest thou God’s high priest?

units.leftText: “Brothers,” Paul replied, “I was not aware that he was the high priest, for it is written: ‘Do not speak evil about the ruler of your people.’ ”
units.rightText: And Paul said, I knew not, brethren, that he was high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of a ruler of thy people.
leftNotes: 23:5 Exodus 22:28|EXO 22:28* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Then Paul, knowing that some of them were Sadducees and the others Pharisees, called out in the Sanhedrin, “Brothers, I am a Pharisee, the son of a Pharisee. It is because of my hope in the resurrection of the dead that I am on trial.”
units.rightText: But when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, Brethren, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees: touching the hope and resurrection of the dead I am called in question.

units.leftText: As soon as he had said this, a dispute broke out between the Pharisees and Sadducees, and the assembly was divided.
units.rightText: And when he had so said, there arose a dissension between the Pharisees and Sadducees; and the assembly was divided.

units.leftText: For the Sadducees say that there is neither a resurrection nor angels nor spirits, but the Pharisees acknowledge them all.
units.rightText: For the Sadducees say that there is no resurrection, neither angel, nor spirit; but the Pharisees confess both.

units.leftText: A great clamor arose, and some scribes from the party of the Pharisees got up and contended sharply, “We find nothing wrong with this man. What if a spirit or an angel has spoken to him?”
units.rightText: And there arose a great clamor: and some of the scribes of the Pharisees’ part stood up, and strove, saying, We find no evil in this man: and what if a spirit hath spoken to him, or an angel?

units.leftText: The dispute grew so violent that the commander was afraid they would tear Paul to pieces. He ordered the soldiers to go down and remove him by force and bring him into the barracks.
units.rightText: And when there arose a great dissension, the chief captain, fearing lest Paul should be torn in pieces by them, commanded the soldiers to go down and take him by force from among them, and bring him into the castle.

units.leftText: The following night the Lord stood near Paul and said, “Take courage! As you have testified about Me in Jerusalem, so also you must testify in Rome.” The Plot to Kill Paul (John 16:1–4|JHN 16:1-4*)
units.rightText: And the night following the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good cheer: for as thou hast testified concerning me at Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.

units.leftText: When daylight came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
units.rightText: And when it was day, the Jews banded together, and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.

units.leftText: More than forty of them were involved in this plot.
units.rightText: And they were more than forty that made this conspiracy.

units.leftText: They went to the chief priests and elders and said, “We have bound ourselves with a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul.
units.rightText: And they came to the chief priests and the elders, and said, We have bound ourselves under a great curse, to taste nothing until we have killed Paul.

units.leftText: Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him down to you on the pretext of examining his case more carefully. We are ready to kill him on the way.”
units.rightText: Now therefore do ye with the council signify to the chief captain that he bring him down unto you, as though ye would judge of his case more exactly: and we, before he comes near, are ready to slay him.

units.leftText: But when the son of Paul’s sister heard about the plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul.
units.rightText: But Paul’s sister’s son heard of their lying in wait, and he came and entered into the castle and told Paul.
leftNotes: 23:16 Or the ambush

units.leftText: Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.”
units.rightText: And Paul called unto him one of the centurions, and said, Bring this young man unto the chief captain; for he hath something to tell him.

units.leftText: So the centurion took him to the commander and said, “Paul the prisoner sent and asked me to bring this young man to you. He has something to tell you.”
units.rightText: So he took him, and brought him to the chief captain, and saith, Paul the prisoner called me unto him, and asked me to bring this young man unto thee, who hath something to say to thee.

units.leftText: The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside, and asked, “What do you need to tell me?”
units.rightText: And the chief captain took him by the hand, and going aside asked him privately, What is it that thou hast to tell me?

units.leftText: He answered, “The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul to the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of acquiring more information about him.
units.rightText: And he said, The Jews have agreed to ask thee to bring down Paul to-morrow unto the council, as though thou wouldest inquire somewhat more exactly concerning him.

units.leftText: Do not let them persuade you, because more than forty men are waiting to ambush him. They have bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him; they are ready now, awaiting your consent.”
units.rightText: Do not thou therefore yield unto them: for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, who have bound themselves under a curse, neither to eat nor to drink till they have slain him: and now are they ready, looking for the promise from thee.

units.leftText: So the commander dismissed the young man and instructed him, “Do not tell anyone that you have reported this to me.” Paul Sent to Felix
units.rightText: So the chief captain let the young man go, charging him, Tell no man that thou hast signified these things to me.

units.leftText: Then he called two of his centurions and said, “Prepare two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen to go to Caesarea in the third hour of the night.
units.rightText: And he called unto him two of the centurions, and said, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go as far as Cæsarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night:
leftNotes: 23:23 That is, at nine tonight

units.leftText: Provide mounts for Paul to take him safely to Governor Felix.”
units.rightText: and he bade them provide beasts, that they might set Paul thereon, and bring him safe unto Felix the governor.

units.leftText: And he wrote the following letter:
units.rightText: And he wrote a letter after this form:

units.leftText: Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency, Governor Felix: Greetings.
units.rightText: Claudius Lysias unto the most excellent governor Felix, greeting.

units.leftText: This man was seized by the Jews, and they were about to kill him when I came with my troops to rescue him. For I had learned that he is a Roman citizen,
units.rightText: This man was seized by the Jews, and was about to be slain of them, when I came upon them with the soldiers and rescued him, having learned that he was a Roman.

units.leftText: and since I wanted to understand their charges against him, I brought him down to their Sanhedrin.
units.rightText: And desiring to know the cause wherefore they accused him, I brought him down unto their council:

units.leftText: I found that the accusation involved questions about their own law, but there was no charge worthy of death or imprisonment.
units.rightText: whom I found to be accused about questions of their law, but to have nothing laid to his charge worthy of death or of bonds.

units.leftText: When I was informed that there was a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once. I also instructed his accusers to present their case against him before you.
units.rightText: And when it was shown to me that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to thee forthwith, charging his accusers also to speak against him before thee.

units.leftText: So the soldiers followed their orders and brought Paul by night to Antipatris.
units.rightText: So the soldiers, as it was commanded them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.

units.leftText: The next day they returned to the barracks and let the horsemen go on with him.
units.rightText: But on the morrow they left the horsemen to go with him, and returned to the castle:

units.leftText: When the horsemen arrived in Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor and presented Paul to him.
units.rightText: and they, when they came to Cæsarea and delivered the letter to the governor, presented Paul also before him.

units.leftText: The governor read the letter and asked what province Paul was from. Learning that he was from Cilicia,
units.rightText: And when he had read it, he asked of what province he was; and when he understood that he was of Cilicia,

units.leftText: he said, “I will hear your case when your accusers arrive.” Then he ordered that Paul be kept under guard in Herod’s Praetorium.
units.rightText: I will hear thee fully, said he, when thine accusers also are come: and he commanded him to be kept in Herod’s palace.

units.leftText: Five days later the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a lawyer named Tertullus, who presented to the governor their case against Paul.
units.rightText: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with certain elders, and with an orator, one Tertullus; and they informed the governor against Paul.
leftNotes: 24:1 Or an orator

units.leftText: When Paul had been called in, Tertullus opened the prosecution: “Because of you, we have enjoyed a lasting peace, and your foresight has brought improvements to this nation.
units.rightText: And when he was called, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, Seeing that by thee we enjoy much peace, and that by thy providence evils are corrected for this nation,

units.leftText: In every way and everywhere, most excellent Felix, we acknowledge this with all gratitude.
units.rightText: we accept it in all ways and in all places, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

units.leftText: But in order not to delay you any further, I beg your indulgence to hear us briefly.
units.rightText: But, that I be not further tedious unto thee, I entreat thee to hear us of thy clemency a few words.

units.leftText: We have found this man to be a pestilence, stirring up dissension among the Jews all over the world. He is a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
units.rightText: For we have found this man a pestilent fellow, and a mover of insurrections among all the Jews throughout the world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes:

units.leftText: and he even tried to desecrate the temple; so we seized him.
units.rightText: who moreover assayed to profane the temple: on whom also we laid hold:
leftNotes: 24:6 TR includes and we would have judged him according to our law. 7*But Lysias the commander came with great force and took him out of our hands, 8*ordering his accusers to come before you.

rightNotes: 24:7 Some ancient authorities insert and we would have judged him according to our law. But the chief captain Lysias came, and with great violence took him away out of our hands, commanding his accusers to come before thee.

units.leftText: By examining him yourself, you will be able to learn the truth about all our charges against him.”
units.rightText: from whom thou wilt be able, by examining him thyself, to take knowledge of all these things whereof we accuse him.

units.leftText: The Jews concurred, asserting that these charges were true. Paul’s Defense to Felix
units.rightText: And the Jews also joined in the charge, affirming that these things were so.

units.leftText: When the governor motioned for Paul to speak, he began his response: “Knowing that you have been a judge over this nation for many years, I gladly make my defense.
units.rightText: And when the governor had beckoned unto him to speak, Paul answered, Forasmuch as I know that thou hast been of many years a judge unto this nation, I cheerfully make my defence:

units.leftText: You can verify for yourself that no more than twelve days ago I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
units.rightText: seeing that thou canst take knowledge that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem:

units.leftText: Yet my accusers did not find me debating with anyone in the temple or riling up a crowd in the synagogues or in the city.
units.rightText: and neither in the temple did they find me disputing with any man or stirring up a crowd, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city.

units.leftText: Nor can they prove to you any of their charges against me.

units.leftText: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
units.rightText: And while the day was coming on, Paul besought them all to take some food, saying, This day is the fourteenth day that ye wait and continue fasting, having taken nothing.

units.leftText: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
units.rightText: Wherefore I beseech you to take some food: for this is for your safety: for there shall not a hair perish from the head of any of you.

units.leftText: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
units.rightText: And when he had said this, and had taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all; and he brake it, and began to eat.

units.leftText: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
units.rightText: Then were they all of good cheer, and themselves also took food.

units.leftText: In all, there were 276 of us on board.
units.rightText: And we were in all in the ship two hundred threescore and sixteen souls.

units.leftText: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
units.rightText: And when they had eaten enough, they lightened the ship, throwing out the wheat into the sea.

units.leftText: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
units.rightText: And when it was day, they knew not the land: but they perceived a certain bay with a beach, and they took counsel whether they could drive the ship upon it.

units.leftText: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
units.rightText: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosing the bands of the rudders; and hoisting up the foresail to the wind, they made for the beach.

units.leftText: But the ship struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
units.rightText: But lighting upon a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground; and the foreship struck and remained unmoveable, but the stern began to break up by the violence of the waves.

units.leftText: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
units.rightText: And the soldiers’ counsel was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim out, and escape.

units.leftText: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
units.rightText: But the centurion, desiring to save Paul, stayed them from their purpose; and commanded that they who could swim should cast themselves overboard, and get first to the land;

units.leftText: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
units.rightText: and the rest, some on planks, and some on other things from the ship. And so it came to pass, that they all escaped safe to the land.

units.leftText: Once we were safely ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
units.rightText: And when we were escaped, then we knew that the island was called Melita.

units.leftText: The islanders showed us extraordinary kindness. They kindled a fire and welcomed all of us because it was raining and cold.
units.rightText: And the barbarians showed us no common kindness: for they kindled a fire, and received us all, because of the present rain, and because of the cold.

units.leftText: Paul gathered a bundle of sticks, and as he laid them on the fire, a viper, driven out by the heat, fastened itself to his hand.
units.rightText: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out by reason of the heat, and fastened on his hand.

units.leftText: When the islanders saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “Surely this man is a murderer. Although he was saved from the sea, Justice has not allowed him to live.”
units.rightText: And when the barbarians saw the venomous creature hanging from his hand, they said one to another, No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he hath escaped from the sea, yet Justice hath not suffered to live.
leftNotes: 28:4 Greek Dike; that is, the Greek goddess of justice

units.leftText: But Paul shook the creature off into the fire and suffered no ill effects.
units.rightText: Howbeit he shook off the creature into the fire, and took no harm.

units.leftText: The islanders were expecting him to swell up or suddenly drop dead. But after waiting a long time and seeing nothing unusual happen to him, they changed their minds and said he was a god.
units.rightText: But they expected that he would have swollen, or fallen down dead suddenly: but when they were long in expectation and beheld nothing amiss come to him, they changed their minds, and said that he was a god.

units.leftText: Nearby stood an estate belonging to Publius, the chief official of the island. He welcomed us and entertained us hospitably for three days.
units.rightText: Now in the neighborhood of that place were lands belonging to the chief man of the island, named Publius; who received us, and entertained us three days courteously.

units.leftText: The father of Publius was sick in bed, suffering from fever and dysentery. Paul went in to see him, and after praying and placing his hands on him, he healed the man.
units.rightText: And it was so, that the father of Publius lay sick of fever and dysentery: unto whom Paul entered in, and prayed, and laying his hands on him healed him.

units.leftText: After this had happened, the rest of the sick on the island came and were cured as well.
units.rightText: And when this was done, the rest also that had diseases in the island came, and were cured:

units.leftText: The islanders honored us in many ways and supplied our needs when we were ready to sail. Paul Arrives in Italy
units.rightText: who also honored us with many honors; and when we sailed, they put on board such things as we needed.

units.leftText: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island. It had the Twin Brothers as a figurehead.
units.rightText: And after three months we set sail in a ship of Alexandria which had wintered in the island, whose sign was The Twin Brothers.
leftNotes: 28:11 Greek Dioscuri; that is, the Greek gods Castor and Pollux

units.leftText: Putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
units.rightText: And touching at Syracuse, we tarried there three days.

units.leftText: From there we weighed anchor and came to Rhegium. After one day, a south wind came up, and on the second day we arrived at Puteoli.
units.rightText: And from thence we made a circuit, and arrived at Rhegium: and after one day a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli;

units.leftText: There we found some brothers who invited us to spend the week with them. And so we came to Rome.
units.rightText: where we found brethren, and were entreated to tarry with them seven days: and so we came to Rome.

units.leftText: The brothers there had heard about us and traveled as far as the Forum of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet us. When Paul saw them, he was encouraged and gave thanks to God. Paul Preaches at Rome (Isaiah 6:1–13|ISA 6:1-13*)
units.rightText: And from thence the brethren, when they heard of us, came to meet us as far as The Market of Appius and The Three Taverns; whom when Paul saw, he thanked God, and took courage.
leftNotes: 28:15 The Forum of Appius was about 43 miles or 70 kilometers from Rome.
28:15 The Three Taverns was about 35 miles or 57 kilometers from Rome.

units.leftText: When we arrived in Rome, Paul was permitted to stay by himself, with a soldier to guard him.
units.rightText: And when we entered into Rome, Paul was suffered to abide by himself with the soldier that guarded him.
leftNotes: 28:16 BYZ and TR include the centurion delivered up the prisoners to the captain of the barrack, but.

units.leftText: After three days, he called together the leaders of the Jews. When they had gathered, he said to them, “Brothers, although I have done nothing against our people or the customs of our fathers, I was taken prisoner in Jerusalem and handed over to the Romans.
units.rightText: And it came to pass, that after three days he called together those that were the chief of the Jews: and when they were come together, he said unto them, I, brethren, though I had done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, yet was delivered prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans:

units.leftText: They examined me and wanted to release me, because there was no basis for a death sentence against me.
units.rightText: who, when they had examined me, desired to set me at liberty, because there was no cause of death in me.

units.leftText: But when the Jews objected, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, even though I have no charge to bring against my nation.
units.rightText: But when the Jews spake against it, I was constrained to appeal unto Cæsar; not that I had aught whereof to accuse my nation.

units.leftText: So for this reason I have called to see you and speak with you. It is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain.”
units.rightText: For this cause therefore did I entreat you to see and to speak with me: for because of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain.

units.leftText: The leaders replied, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea, nor have any of the brothers from there reported or even mentioned anything bad about you.
units.rightText: And they said unto him, We neither received letters from Judæa concerning thee, nor did any of the brethren come hither and report or speak any harm of thee.

units.leftText: But we consider your views worth hearing, because we know that people everywhere are speaking against this sect.”
units.rightText: But we desire to hear of thee what thou thinkest: for as concerning this sect, it is known to us that everywhere it is spoken against.

units.leftText: So they set a day to meet with Paul, and many people came to the place he was staying. He expounded to them from morning to evening, testifying about the kingdom of God and persuading them about Jesus from the Law of Moses and the Prophets.
units.rightText: And when they had appointed him a day, they came to him into his lodging in great number; to whom he expounded the matter, testifying the kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning till evening.

units.leftText: Some of them were convinced by what he said, but others refused to believe.
units.rightText: And some believed the things which were spoken, and some disbelieved.

units.leftText: They disagreed among themselves and began to leave after Paul had made this final statement: “The Holy Spirit was right when He spoke to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet:
units.rightText: And when they agreed not among themselves, they departed after that Paul had spoken one word, Well spake the Holy Spirit through Isaiah the prophet unto your fathers,

units.leftText: ‘Go to this people and say, “You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.”
units.rightText: saying, Go thou unto this people, and say, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall in no wise understand; And seeing ye shall see, and shall in no wise perceive:

units.leftText: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
units.rightText: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, And their ears are dull of hearing, And their eyes they have closed; Lest haply they should perceive with their eyes, And hear with their ears, And understand with their heart, And should turn again, And I should heal them.
leftNotes: 28:27 Isaiah 6:9–10|ISA 6:9-10* (see also LXX)

units.leftText: Be advised, therefore, that God’s salvation has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will listen!”
units.rightText: Be it known therefore unto you, that this salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles: they will also hear.
leftNotes: 28:28 BYZ and TR include 29*When he had said this, the Jews went away, disputing sharply among themselves.

rightNotes: 28:29 Some ancient authorities insert v. 29: And when he had said these words, the Jews departed, having much disputing among themselves.

units.leftText: Paul stayed there two full years in his own rented house, welcoming all who came to visit him.
units.rightText: And he abode two whole years in his own hired dwelling, and received all that went in unto him,

units.leftText: Boldly and freely he proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, none forbidding him.
